articles.title: Festival Transformar em Santos: Programação gratuita até domingo | G1
articles.standfirst: A programação reúne oficinas de fotografia, teatro, gastronomia e sustentabilidade, além de exposições, apresentações culturais e uma feira com mais de 60 marcas. As atividades são gratuitas e acontecem no Sesc Santos e na Praça Dr. Caio Ribeiro de Moraes e Silva, até domingo (15).
articles.summary: O Festival Transformar Santos oferece oficinas de fotografia, gastronomia e feira criativa com 60 marcas na Praça Dr. Caio Ribeiro e no Sesc até este domingo.
articles.body:
Também será possível participar de uma oficina que acompanhará os bastidores do 'Documentário Transformar' — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Santos

A cidade de Santos , no litoral de São Paulo, recebe até domingo (15) a terceira edição do Festival Transformar, com programação gratuita voltada à cultura, educação, sustentabilidade e economia criativa. Entre as atrações, há oficinas, apresentações culturais, exposições e uma feira com mais de 60 marcas.

Idealizado por Gabriel Del Corso e realizado pela Re-Set.br, o festival tem o apoio do Senac Santos e do Sesc Santos. O Instituto Brasileiro de Defesa da Natureza (IBDN) é parceiro nas ações de neutralização de carbono.

A programação começou na quarta-feira (11), com atividades no Sesc Santos, no bairro Aparecida, e na Praça Dr. Caio Ribeiro de Moraes e Silva. Entre os destaques, estão oficinas de fotografia, teatro, customização de roupas, gastronomia e alimentação saudável.

As atividades são gratuitas e têm vagas limitadas. A programação é dividida entre o Sesc Santos, na Rua Conselheiro Ribas, nº 136, e a Praça Dr. Caio Ribeiro de Moraes e Silva, ambos no bairro Aparecida.

As inscrições para as oficinas do Senac estão disponíveis no site da instituição. As demais atividades têm inscrições e condições específicas de participação.

O núcleo Mar Aberto — Futuros em Circulação oferece atividades em diferentes áreas. Confira alguns dos temas:

Customização de roupas e reaproveitamento de tecidos;

Culinária caiçara e alimentação saudável;

Laboratório audiovisual para produção de minidocumentários;

Painel sobre desenvolvimento sustentável e governança colaborativa.

Até sábado (14), das 11h às 21h, a Praça Dr. Caio Ribeiro de Moraes e Silva recebe o núcleo Viva Circular, com mais de 60 marcas de gastronomia, arte, moda, design e outros segmentos.

O espaço também terá exposições, música, atividades culturais gratuitas e iniciativas de afroempreendedorismo do Coletivo AfroTu.

articles.title: MC Hariel declara independência com o álbum 'Aplauso não paga as contas' | G1
articles.body:
MC Hariel afirma que revê a trajetória no funk ao longo das 13 faixas do álbum 'Aplauso não paga as contas' — Foto: Renan Miranda / Divulgação

♬ A caminho dos 29 anos, a serem festejados em 20 de dezembro, MC Hariel zera o jogo com a edição do álbum “Aplauso não paga as contas”, em rotação nos aplicativos de áudio desde sexta-feira, 13 de dezembro.

Doze anos após ter ganhado projeção no universo do funk ao pôr em campo a música “Passei sorrindo” (2014), Haniel Denaro Ribeiro declara a independência artística.

O artista saiu da produtora GR6 após 12 anos e abriu a empresa Zaori em 2025 para gerir a própria carreira em sincronia com a gravadora que criou em 2024, Xaolin Records, selo fonográfico que Hariel mantém em associação com a Warner Music, companhia fonográfica que edita os lançamentos do artista desde 2021.

É essa gravadora que distribui no mercado digital o álbum “Aplauso não paga as contas”, com o qual o MC paulistano afirma revisar a trajetória no universo do funk ao longo de 13 faixas gravadas com produção musical de nomes como André Nine, DJ Perera (colaborador de Hariel desde os tempos do já mencionado primeiro single de sucesso do artista, “Passei sorrindo”), Deejhay Luh, Ecologik, Fejuca, DK Kaio Mix, LT no Beat, Murilo e Pdrin.

O álbum “Aplauso não paga as contas” sucede o EP “A Vida é um Freestyle” (2026), lançado em 16 de abril como o primeiro movimento de independência de Hariel.

Com 15 anos de carreira iniciada de forma caseira em 2011, o MC agrega no álbum “Aplauso não paga as contas” os quatro participantes vitoriosos – MC Campos, MC Coutto, MC Dan e Kisha Zo – do concurso de freestyle que promoveu no embalo do lançamento do EP anterior.

Kisha Zo figura na faixa “Questão de tempo”. MC Campos & MC Dan unem vozes em “Só tá sem amor”. Já MC Coutto é o convidado de “Rakeada”.

“Eu vim da periferia e sei que existe muito talento ali, mas, muitas vezes, falta oportunidade para esse talento aparecer. Esse concurso foi uma forma de abrir uma porta para quem acompanha meu trabalho e sonha em viver de música, assim como eu sonhei um dia. Ver esses quatro fãs entrarem no estúdio, participarem do processo e terem suas faixas no álbum mostra que, quando a oportunidade é real, ela pode mudar caminhos”, argumenta Hariel no texto de apresentação do álbum “Aplauso não paga as contas”.

MC Lkazin e Gblack, artistas da nova geração do elenco da produtora GR6, completam o time de convidados de MC Hariel no álbum, antecedido em 29 de outubro pela edição do single com a música “Outono”. Lkazin aparece na faixa “Maloqueiro e sonhador”. Já Gblack participa da música “Imaginando”.

articles.title: Paulliny Tort: Livro Os Imortais terá filme de Rodrigo Teixeira | G1
articles.standfirst: Paulliny Tort conquistou prêmios nacionais com obra. História narra drama protagonizado por neandertais, e inclui um encontro com a espécie humana como conhecemos.
articles.summary: O premiado livro Os Imortais, de Paulliny Tort, será adaptado para o cinema pela RT Features, de Rodrigo Teixeira, mesmo produtor do sucesso Ainda Estou Aqui.
articles.body:
Paulliny Tort — Foto: Renato Parada/Divulgação

Após vencer o Prêmio Literário Biblioteca Nacional, a escritora brasiliense Paulliny Tort vai estrear no cinema com o romance Os Imortais (2026), publicado pela Editora Fósforo.

A obra será adaptada para o cinema pela RT Features, do premiado produtor Rodrigo Teixeira , um dos nomes responsáveis pela adaptação de "Ainda estou aqui" .

Em outubro, o livro – que narra o drama de um grupo de neandertais em busca de sobrevivência – venceu a premiação da Biblioteca Nacional na categoria romance.

🏆 Paulliny compartilha o prêmio com autores estreantes e nomes ilustres da literatura brasileira, como Adélia Prado, vencedora na categoria poesia, e Maria Valéria Rezende, em contos.

Nas redes sociais, a produtora contou que a obra já está em desenvolvimento.

A ideia começou do encantamento de Rodrigo pela obra.

“Eu fiquei maravilhado quando li este livro. Paulliny Tort entrega uma dimensão épica em cada palavra e, ao mesmo tempo, aborda questões universais sobre a humanidade, e isso torna esse projeto especialmente instigante para nós. Não poderíamos estar mais entusiasmados em levar essa história para o cinema", diz o produtor.

O cineasta afirma ainda que a obra consolida a trajetória da RT com adaptações literárias.

Uma das mais famosas é a versão de "Me chame pelo seu nome" (2017) . O livro, do escritor André Aciman, deu origem ao longa de 2017 protagonizado por Armie Hammer e Thimotée Chalamet e vencedor do Oscar de Melhor Roteiro Adaptado em 2018.

A produtora também encerrou, neste ano, as gravações de "Zero K" , adaptação do romance homônimo do americano Don DeLillo. E se prepara para adaptar "Não fossem as sílabas do sábado" , da brasileira Mariana Salomão Carrara.

"É um romance extraordinário em muitos sentidos, e a adaptação terá o desafio, mas também o privilégio, de manejar essas particularidades a favor do formado audiovisual. Tenho certeza de que o Rodrigo Teixeira e a equipe da RT são os parceiros ideais para essa empreitada, pela combinação perfeita que eles fazem entre ousadia e sensibilidade", destacou Rita Mattar, sócia-fundadora da editora.

Passada no período de surgimento da espécie humana como conhecemos, ' Os Imortais' narra a história na perspectiva do Homem, um neandertal que chefia o próprio grupo na luta por sobrevivência .

Em meio a caçadas e confrontos para garantir a segurança da própria espécie, o personagem é atravessado pelo luto pelos que ficam no caminho e o medo do desconhecido.

O ponto de virada da história ocorre quando o grupo de neandertais encontram uma comunidade de outros seres humanos, mas com formas físicas e hábitos que causam estranhamento pelas diferenças. As espécies coexistiram há cerca de 40 mil anos.

“Eu costumo dizer que eu não fiz uma pesquisa para o livro. Mesmo antes da universidade, mesmo quando eu era criança, adolescente, eu já lia sobre. Daí, quando eu chego para escrever uma história, tem esse background”, conta a escritora.

“Todo o esforço da literatura é sobre a experiência de estar vivo, o que a gente sente diante da experiência de estar vivo. A experiência da vida impacta não só nós, pessoas. Então, seja um neandertal, ou seja um grupo de crianças em situação de rua como Jorge Amado [em 'Capitães de areia'], ou mesmo uma autoficção, ele sempre vai passar por esses sentimentos, esses estranhamentos, os encantamentos da vida”, afirma.

Um dos desafios da adaptação para as telas deve ser a linguagem — ou a falta dela.

No livro, a "não palavra" está presente nos olhares e gestos das personagens, que se comunicam sem precisar dizer. Afinal, a linguagem como conhecemos só seria criada depois.

"Tem um autor que eu gosto muito [Steven Pinker], que traz vários exemplos de como a nossa mente funciona em duas frentes. Pensamento e linguagem são coisas entrelaçadas, mas que evoluem separadamente. Se o pensamento carecesse de linguagem para existir, nunca existiriam palavras novas", pontua.

Para a escritora, as obras surgem de uma cena, a partir da qual ela desenvolve sem saber no que vai dar. Em "Os imortais", a imagem foi a de um neandertal caçando um javali.

“Eu sentei, comecei a trabalhar, gostei da imagem. Fui ficando, fui me envolvendo com o personagem. E aos poucos, ele foi me apresentando o resto da história”, contou ao g1.

Os Imortais, de Paulliny Tort. Editora Fósforo, 2026. — Foto: Divulgação

“Eu escrevo com o prazer da descoberta, eu quero saber aonde a história vai me levar. Às vezes, eu até sei aonde ela vai me levar, mas não como ela vai me levar. Quando eu estou escrevendo, eu posso até saber o que vai acontecer, mas não sei como, vou descobrir escrevendo”, afirma.

✍️ Mas a escrita não é feita de um “momento de inspiração”.

A autora destaca que a escrita tem uma série de ferramentas. É necessário estudar temas, ler referências, assistir coisas novas e tudo aquilo que estimule a criação.

Atualmente, Paulliny se dedica exclusivamente à escrita e defende o reconhecimento da profissão.

“Todas as linguagens artísticas merecem um status de trabalho. A gente tem que tratar essas pessoas com dignidade na sociedade, porque o que elas oferecem para a gente é precioso também”, pontua.

Para a escritora, a literatura brasileira vive um momento de “menos timidez” . Há um movimento de maior interesse dos leitores e mais procura de escritores para publicação.

Segundo levantamento feito pela Câmara Brasileira do Livro, o Brasil ganhou 3 milhões de leitores entre 2024 e 2025.

“A visibilidade para a literatura contemporânea aumentou, a gente tem clubes de leitura, tem esse movimento de ler mulheres, que eu acho que também ajudou muito. Não só mulheres, mas, por exemplo, o Itamar [Vieira Junior], que é um fenômeno da literatura nacional, tem revistas especializadas. Então, eu acho que tem gente querendo ler autores e autoras brasileiras cada vez mais”, comenta.

A tendência, aponta a autora, é que esse número cresça ainda mais. Para isso, no entanto, Paulliny defende que haja políticas de incentivo.

Uma das ações é o MEC Livros, iniciativa do Ministério da Educação que dá acesso a livros digitais de forma gratuita. Paulliny comenta que o projeto ainda apresenta uma série de fatores a serem melhorados, como a remuneração de autores e os processos de seleção das obras, mas é um passo importante.

“Existem diferentes tipos de livros para diferentes tipos de pessoas. O importante é que existam políticas públicas para o livro e para a leitura, isso eu acho que é indispensável”, finaliza.

articles.title: 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' box office collection day 10: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash's film earns over 3 times 'Animal'; crosses Rs 1,200 cr worldwide; Hindi version leads
articles.summary: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash's 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' continues its impressive theatrical run, recording a major jump in collections on its second
articles.body: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash's 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' continues its impressive theatrical run, recording a major jump in collections on its second Saturday. The mythological epic collected Rs 72.90 cr net in India on Day 10, registering a 51.6% rise over the previous day's earnings. With this, the film's domestic net collection has reached Rs 685.60 cr, while its India gross stands at Rs 819.50 cr. The film has also crossed the Rs 1,200 cr milestone worldwide, with its cumulative gross collection reaching Rs 1,228 cr.Ramayana Movie Review'Ramayana' Day 10 box office collection across languagesAccording to Sacnilk, the Hindi version remained the biggest contributor to the film's Saturday earnings. It collected Rs 53.75 cr from 18,557 shows. The Kannada version followed with Rs 5.40 cr from 893 screenings. Both Malayalam and Tamil versions earned Rs 4.75 cr each, from 1,127 and 1,290 shows, respectively. Telugu contributed another Rs 4.25 cr through 1,584 screenings.Across all five languages, the film registered an overall occupancy of 45.5% on Saturday. Malayalam recorded the highest occupancy at 83%, followed by Tamil at 62.5% and Kannada at 58.8%. Hindi registered 41.9%, while Telugu recorded 39.1%.For the Hindi 3D version, overall occupancy stood at 53%. Morning shows recorded 30.08%, while afternoon screenings reached 57.08%. Evening shows registered 62.77% occupancy, followed by 62.08% during the night.'Ramayana' worldwide box office collection crosses Rs 1,200 crThe film's overseas performance has further strengthened its global box office position. International markets contributed Rs 30 cr on Day 10, taking the cumulative overseas gross to Rs 408.50 cr. Combined with its domestic gross, the worldwide collection has reached Rs 1,228 cr, according to Sacnilk.The domestic market accounts for 66.7% of the worldwide earnings, while overseas territories contribute the remaining 33.3%. The film's average collection per show on Saturday was Rs 32,454. Its latest performance also marks a considerable improvement over Friday, when it earned Rs 48.10 cr net in India.'Ramayana' box office collection: Day-wise performance'Ramayana' began its theatrical journey on November 5 with Rs 64.85 cr net in India. After collecting Rs 48.05 cr on Friday, the film recovered on Saturday with Rs 69.80 cr. Sunday brought in Rs 56.15 cr before Monday delivered its biggest single-day collection of Rs 107.50 cr.The film subsequently earned Rs 94.10 cr on Tuesday and Rs 70.65 cr on Wednesday. Its first Thursday collection stood at Rs 53.50 cr. The opening eight-day run generated Rs 564.60 cr net and Rs 675.05 cr gross domestically.Friday's earnings during the second week stood at Rs 48.10 cr. Saturday's improved performance pushed the two-day second-week total to Rs 121 cr net and Rs 144.45 cr gross. The Hindi version has contributed Rs 527.25 cr to the domestic net collection so far, accounting for 76.9% of the total. Kannada follows with Rs 57.35 cr, while Telugu has generated Rs 44.90 cr. Tamil and Malayalam have contributed Rs 29.65 cr and Rs 26.45 cr, respectively.Ranbir Kapoor's 'Ramayana' earns over three times 'Animal'The latest figures also put the film ahead of Ranbir Kapoor's previous release, 'Animal', at the same stage of its theatrical run. Directed by Sandeep Reddy Vanga, the action drama collected Rs 36 cr net in India on its tenth day. This is less than half of 'Ramayana's' corresponding domestic earnings.'Animal' recorded Rs 33.53 cr from its Hindi version, with 12,949 shows. Telugu contributed Rs 2.13 cr through 1,168 screenings, while Tamil added Rs 30 lakh from 222 shows. Kannada and Malayalam each earned Rs 2 lakh, from 17 and 34 screenings, respectively.By Day 10, 'Animal' had accumulated Rs 431.27 cr net and Rs 514.05 cr gross in India. Its overseas gross stood at Rs 203.25 cr, including Rs 13.75 cr from the tenth day. The worldwide gross collection reached Rs 717.30 cr. Its second-week earnings had reached Rs 93.69 cr, with the tenth day contributing Rs 36 cr.About 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend''Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' brings the timeless Indian epic about Lord Rama and King Ravana to the screen through a contemporary cinematic adaptation. The story has influenced generations and remains deeply rooted in India's cultural traditions.The first instalment focuses on Prince Rama's early life and the challenges he encounters as the rightful heir to Ayodhya. Headlined by Ranbir Kapoor and Yash, the ambitious film revisits the legendary narrative through modern Indian cinema.DISCLAIMER: The box office numbers and the data in this article are compiled from public and industry sources. articles.title: Parenting advice by Khloé Kardashian: 'It's so important for kids to know, to see how adults trip or fail a little bit,' reveals the diva, explaining how she stopped her daughter from quitting gymnastics
articles.summary: Discover how Khloé Kardashian inspired her daughter True to keep pursuing gymnastics despite struggles, emphasizing the importance of showing kids that even adults can fail and learn.
articles.body: Khloé Kardashian wasn't about to let her daughter give up gymnastics over one cartwheel. True, who is eight, was frustrated because she couldn't nail the move, and she kept comparing herself to her cousins, who seemed to be doing much better. So Khloé came up with a plan. She'd try a cartwheel herself, fully expecting to fail at it too.She told the story on an episode of her podcast, Khloé in Wonder Land, with actor Goldie Hawn as her guest. They were discussing parenting and kids' confidence, and Khloé described how her own clumsy attempt ended up changing True's mind.Why did True Thompson want to quit gymnastics?According to Khloé Kardashian, True was thinking about giving up because her cousins could do the cartwheel better than she could. It was really getting to her, especially watching the other kids manage something she was stuck on.So Khloé said she'd go to gymnastics and try as well. She wanted True to see that even grown-ups can't do everything, and that nothing is embarrassing about that. Here's how she remembered putting it to her daughter: "Girl, do you want to? Okay. I'm going to go to gymnastics with you. I'm going to do a cartwheel because I can't do one. And I'm going to show her that an adult can't do this. And you're going to be fine."Khloé Kardashian's cartwheel attempt made True more confidentShe did go through with it, and it sounds like it didn't go to plan. She was laughing about it on the podcast, saying, "So I did a cartwheel the best I could. It was silly. I looked ridiculous."That was enough to make True feel better about her own effort. Watching her mum struggle with the same move made her realise she wasn't as bad at it as she'd thought.And it worked. Khloé Kardashian said True kept going with gymnastics for another three years after that. In her words: "She now has been in gymnastics three years longer because she saw how ridiculous I looked and she looked way better than me. So she has all this confidence."Khloé Kardashian on why parents should let children see them failThe chat with Goldie Hawn moved on to why parents don't need to look perfect in front of their children. Khloé Kardashian thinks kids should see adults mess up and, just as importantly, see what they do next. She said, "It's so important, I think, for kids to know, to see how adults trip or fail a little bit. Like, how do we handle that?"The gymnastics story is a pretty good example. She didn't give True another pep talk about trying harder. She just made herself the example, couldn't do the cartwheel either, and was happy to laugh at herself about it.Khloé Kardashian says daughter True won't get social media anytime soonKhloé Kardashian also talked about the rules she's set around phones and social media. True is eight and doesn't have a phone, and Khloé has no plans to let her on social media any time soon. "My daughter's only eight, but she's not getting social media for a very long time. She doesn't even have a phone," she said.She also sounded a bit baffled by how young some kids are when they get their first phone. "Kids these days have phones at eight. I'm like, who are you calling? I don't understand," she added.Khloé shares True and her four-year-old son, Tatum Thompson, with her ex Tristan Thompson. She's talked about different parts of raising the two of them before, and this time it was one small moment from True's gymnastics classes that came up.Khloé didn't get the cartwheel, but True got something out of watching her try. She stuck with gymnastics, and her mum came away with a pretty funny story.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.summary: Blake Lively’s beverage business is reportedly heading towards closure, nearly five years after the actress introduced her drinks venture.
articles.body: Blake Lively’s beverage business is reportedly heading towards closure, nearly five years after the actress introduced her drinks venture. The company operates Betty Buzz, a non-alcoholic beverage brand, and its alcoholic counterpart, Betty Booze. Recent developments surrounding the business have raised questions about its future, including inactive social media accounts and changes to its trademark portfolio.According to PEOPLE, the company is winding down its operations and is expected to cease business. The Betty Buzz website is no longer accessible, while the Betty Booze website remained operational as of November 10. The latter continues to showcase its products, although the overall status of the business remains unclear.The reported development follows a series of changes involving the company's online presence and intellectual property filings. While these developments have fuelled speculation about a possible shutdown, the available reports alone do not confirm that the business has officially closed.Beverage venture face uncertain futureBlake Lively launched the beverage venture with two distinct product lines. Both brands were introduced as part of the actress's move into the consumer products market.However, the company's digital presence has changed considerably. The Betty Buzz website is now unavailable, while Betty Booze continues to maintain an active website. The difference has attracted attention amid reports that the business is preparing to wind down.PEOPLE reported that the company is expected to stop operating. Neither the continued availability of the Betty Booze website nor the status of its products necessarily indicates that the brand will remain in business.Several trademark applications abandonedTMZ reported on November 4 that multiple trademark applications associated with Blake Lively's beverage company had been abandoned. The filings were made after the business was launched and covered several categories of products.These included beer-based beverages, non-alcoholic carbonated drinks and other products. However, the trademarks for Betty Buzz and Betty Booze remain active, according to the report.For the unversed, abandoned applications do not automatically mean that a company has ceased operations. Likewise, active registrations for the two principal brands do not establish whether their products will continue to be sold.Instagram accounts show reduced activityThe company's social media presence has also become less frequent. Betty Booze's Instagram account last published an update on September 28, 2026. Betty Buzz's account has been inactive since April 5, 2026.The lack of recent posts, combined with the Betty Buzz website becoming inaccessible, has prompted further questions about the brands' operations. Justin Baldoni legal battle draws attentionThe reported wind-down comes amid Blake Lively's ongoing legal dispute with actor-director Justin Baldoni, her co-star in 'It Ends With Us'. The case has generated considerable public attention, and the negative publicity surrounding the actress is believed to have affected the beverage business.An internal document that became public during the legal proceedings reportedly showed significant sales declines for both Betty Buzz and Betty Booze in August 2024. The figures highlighted the commercial difficulties faced by the brands during that period.According to Inc., retail buyers had also expressed concerns about the potential impact of the controversy surrounding Lively on the beverage lines. While the extent of the damage to sales remains unclear, the reported concerns suggest that the publicity became a factor in how retailers viewed the business.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Former DC head James Gunn shuts down 'Man of Tomorrow' editing rumours, says no Skydance executive has seen the film: 'Any stories around this narrative are false'
articles.summary: James Gunn refutes rumors that Skydance executives demanded changes to the upcoming Superman sequel 'Man of Tomorrow', confirming they haven't seen the film yet.
articles.body: James Gunn has pushed back on rumours about his upcoming DC film 'Man of Tomorrow'. Reports had been circulating that Skydance executives watched the Superman sequel and asked for big changes, but Gunn says that simply isn’t true. As he put it, no one from the company has seen the movie yet, so there’s been no screening and no notes.Gunn addressed the discussion in a post on Threads on November 13, following the announcement that he and Peter Safran would step away from their leadership positions at DC Studios. The news raised questions among fans about the future of projects developed under their management, particularly the next chapter of Superman's story.“There are a lot of untrue rumours going around, but one of them is that Skydance has seen ‘Man of Tomorrow’ and that all sorts of sweeping changes are being made,” Gunn wrote.“No one from Skydance has even seen the movie – the only people that have are Peter Safran and a very small trusted group of friends and family. So any stories around this narrative are false. ”What rumours surrounded 'Man of Tomorrow'?Speculation about the film intensified after reports suggested that the incoming studio leadership could request significant changes to Gunn's sequel. Online discussions included claims about possible reshoots, removed character appearances, and changes to the filmmaker's creative control.Some of the rumours also raised questions about the involvement of characters connected to the wider DC Universe, including Supergirl and Blue Beetle. However, these claims were not confirmed by DC Studios or Skydance.Gunn's response specifically addressed the suggestion that Skydance executives had already watched the film and ordered a major overhaul. By saying who has actually seen the film, Gunn shot down that narrative. He didn’t promise anything about future studio decisions, but he did push back on claims that executives had already stepped into the editing process.Why are James Gunn and Peter Safran leaving DC Studios?The rumours surfaced at a significant time for DC Studios. Big news landed on November 9: Skydance announced that Gunn and Peter Safran are leaving their posts after four years in charge of the division. They’ll officially be out on December 1, 2026. Former Marvel Studios executive Jeremy Latcham will take over as president and chief creative officer. He will oversee the studio's film, television and animation projects and report to Skydance Motion Picture Group co-chairs Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein.In its official announcement, Skydance said Gunn and Safran would return full-time to their creative work. Gunn and Safran also said they still want to keep telling stories they care about, including the next chapter of Clark Kent and Lex Luthor’s story in 'Man of Tomorrow'.Their departure from executive positions does not mean they are leaving the film behind. Gunn remains its writer and director, while he and Safran are attached as producers.What is 'Man of Tomorrow' about?'Man of Tomorrow' is the follow-up to Gunn’s 2025 film 'Superman'. It continues Clark Kent and Lex Luthor’s story, with the two rivals teaming up against a bigger threat. David Corenswet returns as Superman, and Nicholas Hoult is back as Lex Luthor.The film also introduces Lars Eidinger as Brainiac, a major antagonist from DC Comics. Rachel Brosnahan is returning as Lois Lane, alongside other familiar faces from the previous film.The production completed principal photography in August 2026, with Gunn confirming the wrap through his social media. The film is now in post-production and is scheduled to arrive in theatres on July 9, 2027, according to the official announcement.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Black women's swimming documentary Swim Sistas Oscar-longlisted
articles.summary: Cat White says it is "just the most beautiful feeling" to see her film so well received.
articles.body:
The director of a documentary that honours the "powerful celebration of black British women's relationship with water" has been longlisted for an Oscar.

Cat White, from Northampton, said the 11-minute film Swim Sistas could make it to the final nominations for the Best Documentary Short Film at the 99th Academy Awards.

She said it was "just the most beautiful feeling" to see it so well received.

It features Jasmine Boatswain , also from the town, who appeared in the second series of Traitors. She said it was "insane" that an uplifting film about freedom and women's empowerment was getting so much attention.

The film took a day to shoot with a budget of £5,000 and was narrated by the Oscar-nominated actor Naomie Harris.

It also features Alice Dearing, the first black woman to represent Team GB in swimming at an Olympic Games, athlete Lexi Sandiford and Roni Bruno who learned to swim at 54.

White said the film was a tiny idea that was a true "labour of love". It grew from her love of early morning swimming during the Covid-19 pandemic after she suffered a double bereavement.

She said: "I found that the water gave me a sense of peace and healing in a time where it was kind of impossible to get that closure."

She said a further reason to make the film was that Swim England statistics showed about 5% of black adults in the United Kingdom regularly swim.

"It just completely stopped me in my tracks and I began to ask what would it look like if more people who look like me could experience this joy that I get from the water and I built this community around me", she added.

"What better way to change the narrative than by putting them in a film and telling the world about them?"

The film has won several awards including Best Documentary at Northampton Film Festival. It was also the Jury's Choice Award at the Academy Award-qualifying Thomas Edison Film Festival, Best Documentary at the BAFTA and BIFA-qualifying Women X Film Festival and Best Short Film at Kendal Mountain Festival.

It also featured at the inaugural United Nations Swimmable Cities Summit in Rotterdam and was being incorporated into the French national curriculum.

Boatswain said making the film with her family friend was "really special".

She said: "It's a film about breaking outside of the binary - I guess the box you've been put into."

As well as being a swimming enthusiast, Boatswain also used to play rugby for Old Northamptonians and was "the only girl on the rugby team".

She said: "When I tell people that I can swim, that I enjoy the water and going on holiday and jumping out into the sea, people seem quite shocked [and say] 'Oh you can do that' - yes I can.

"I never thought that I'd be involved in anything in my life that would be Oscar adjacent, it's incredible."

She added that White had an "absolutely brilliant mind".

White said it was a "massive boost" that Wunmi Mosaku , who won a BAFTA for Damiola, A Loved Boy and was Oscar-nominated for Sinners, had now joined her as an executive producer.

"I'm developing the project into a wider series where we explore stories around the world, Africa, the Caribbean, the US, black women's stories with water, but I'm interested in Asian women's stories with water, men's stories with water."

She said at a screening in New York someone came up to her and said they had been inspired to "go and learn to swim - which brought it all home".

articles.title: Bowen Yang returns to ‘SNL’ to play ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Former “Saturday Night Live” repertory player and writer Bowen Yang returned to help open the show this weekend with his portrayal of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
articles.body: Former “Saturday Night Live” repertory player and writer Bowen Yang returned to help open the show this weekend with his portrayal of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. In the cold open, the nation’s most-prominent tech-industry CEOs, including Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg, are at a CIA gathering devised to teach them how to identify when a woman may be duping them. “America needs you to learn the difference between a woman who would actually want to have sex with you and a woman who is clearly a spy,” said a CIA guide, portrayed by comedian John Mulaney, the night’s host. Mulaney, a former “SNL” writer, used the story of Huang, who resigned from Nvidia on Thursday following reports that he had extramarital relationships, including one with a suspected spy for China. “What do you think the lesson is here?” Mulaney asked. Zuckerberg, portrayed by Andrew Dismukes, answered: “Never date a human woman.” Mulaney dismissed the response and that of a few of the other tech titans in the room, prompting PayPal cofounder Peter Thiel, portrayed by James Austin Johnson, to defend the group. “Show us some respect,” he said. “We do a lot for this country. Name one time technology has let us down.” Mulaney answered by mentioning Friday’s nationwide flight ground stop and Thursday’s global Microsoft glitch. He tried to empathize, however, noting that it’s a rare time in human history when men “as pale and as strange as you” even survive, let alone possess “all the world’s wealth and power.” Mulaney asked the group to remember the people they dated before they were rich and famous. “Now all of a sudden someone very beautiful is interested in you. Why do you think that might be?” he said. Zuckerberg chimed in. “Because she’s comforted by my Meta glasses recording her at all times.” “No,” Mulaney said. He later introduces someone “who learned this lesson the hard way.” Enter Huang. “It’s me, Jensen ‘Hide Your Wife’ Huang,” Yang said. He explained that he’s into BDSM — “breakin’ da stock market” — and urged the men not to be like him. “Women don’t like guys like us,” he said. “That’s how we became guys like us.” Yang appeared in a subsequent sketch, “Little Park of Horrors,” a spoof of Broadway musicals, that centered on the city outlawing horse-drawn carriages and the two men (Marcello Hernández and Kam Patterson) who want to ride in one. Eventually realizing the dangers and limitations, the pair opt for a vehicle ride in the Lincoln Tunnel only to be confronted by Yang’s Mary Todd Lincoln, who sang about the pitfalls of such a subterranean journey. “No way it’s taking less than two hours,” Lincoln sang. “ ... And it won’t be for free. I’m sayin,’ I’m sayin’ that you and you and you — you’re going to pay me.” A fan favorite, Yang started as a writer in 2018 and joined the cast the next year. He left “SNL” in December 2025, and made his Broadway debut in September as Lincoln in playwright Cole Escola’s “Oh, Mary!” The night’s musical guest was Phoebe Bridgers. “SNL” airs on NBC, a division of NBCUniversal, which is also the parent company of NBC News.

articles.title: 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend': Nitesh Tiwari responds to criticism of Sai Pallavi's action scenes as Sita; cites 'Adbhuta Ramayana' and 'Bilanka Ramayana'
articles.summary: Director Nitesh Tiwari has responded to the criticism surrounding Sai Pallavi's portrayal of Sita in 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend'.
articles.body: Director Nitesh Tiwari has responded to the criticism surrounding Sai Pallavi's portrayal of Sita in 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend'. The actress's action sequences have triggered discussions, with some viewers questioning the creative decision to present the mythological character as a warrior.Addressing the debate, Nitesh Tiwari has explained that his interpretation is based on lesser-known versions of the Ramayana. He cited ancient and regional literary traditions that describe Sita as a powerful manifestation of divine energy. However, actor Mukesh Khanna has expressed a contrasting opinion, arguing that the portrayal does not align with his understanding of the character.Nitesh Tiwari explains the inspiration behind warrior SitaIn an interview with The Federal, Nitesh Tiwari discussed the references that influenced his approach to Sita's character. He pointed towards the Sanskrit text 'Adbhuta Ramayana' and the 15th-century Odia work 'Bilanka Ramayana'. According to the filmmaker, these versions present Sita differently from the familiar depiction of her as a figure defined primarily by endurance and sacrifice.“These tellings offer a rather different image of Sita: not merely a figure of endurance but an active warrior and an embodiment of cosmic Shakti.”The director explained that these literary traditions provided the foundation for portraying Sita with a more active role in the battle against evil. He maintained that the interpretation was not an entirely new concept introduced for modern audiences.Sita takes Mahakali's form to defeat Sahasra RavanaNitesh Tiwari further referred to an episode in which Sita transforms into Mahakali to confront Sahasra Ravana, a thousand-headed demon king. The narrative describes the incident taking place when Rama is incapacitated and unable to defeat the powerful adversary himself.“In these versions, she assumes the fierce form of Mahakali and slays Sahasra Ravana, the thousand-headed demon king, when Rama is incapacitated,” he said.Mukesh Khanna criticises Sai Pallavi's action sequencesMeanwhile, actor Mukesh Khanna has questioned the decision to show Sai Pallavi performing action sequences as Sita. He argued that the character's traditional representation should not be altered to accommodate contemporary interpretations. Interestingly, the actor clarified that he had not watched the movie. His reaction was based on discussions and reviews circulating on social media.As quoted by Kerala Kaumudi, Mukesh Khanna said, "To the best of my knowledge, Valmiki's Ramayana does not mention Sita fighting in a battle anywhere. Sita, the wife of Maryada Purushottam Shri Ram, was a symbol of devotion and sacrifice."'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' features Ranbir Kapoor as Rama, Yash as Ravana and Sai Pallavi as Sita. The ensemble cast also includes Ravi Dubey, Anupam Kher, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Kunal Kapoor, Adinath Kothare, Arun Govil, Indira Krishnan and Lara Dutta.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Sonakshi Sinha morphed photos case: Mumbai court holds Delhi arrest illegal, says, 'The record does not disclose satisfactory compliance'
articles.summary: A Mumbai court on Saturday freed a man who was picked up in Delhi over the alleged circulation of morphed nude pictures of actor Sonakshi Sinha.
articles.body: A Mumbai court on Saturday freed a man who was picked up in Delhi over the alleged circulation of morphed nude pictures of actor Sonakshi Sinha. The magistrate at the Bandra court held that the arrest was illegal because police did not follow the required legal steps while bringing him to Mumbai.Case filed after actor’s complaintAccording to the India Today report, the case was registered on Friday at Bandra police station in Mumbai. Sonakshi Sinha had complained that a person based in Delhi had shared doctored images of her on social media.Arrest in Delhi and journey to MumbaiThe accused, named as Aryan Deepak Jain, was taken into custody at about 10.11 am on Saturday from Jagatpuri Police Station in Delhi’s Shahdara area. He was then flown to Mumbai and presented before a magistrate at the Bandra court. The magistrate, however, ordered his release.Court flags lapse in procedureThe court noted that Aryan Deepak Jain was not first produced before the nearest magistrate in Delhi before being taken out of that jurisdiction. It observed:"Thus, it appears that the police have directly brought the accused from Delhi before this Court without following the procedure of production before the nearest Magistrate,” the court observed.The court also said the investigators had given no satisfactory reason for skipping this step.Police wanted three days of custodyBandra police had asked for three days of custody. They said they needed time to find the device or medium used to create the morphed image and to take the probe forward.Defence opposes custodyAryan Deepak Jain’s lawyers, Aman Shahi, Prashant Trivedi and Aditya Jain, strongly objected. They argued that the arrest broke mandatory safeguards, as police had neither served a notice nor told him the grounds for his arrest. They added that he was brought to Mumbai by air without being presented before a local magistrate.The defence also claimed the police acted in unusual haste because of the complainant’s influential position. Jain maintained that he had committed no offence and that the sections applied in the case did not prima facie fit the facts.Safeguards under BNSS not metThe magistrate observed that the offences carry a jail term of up to seven years. The court said:“Therefore, the investigating officer was required to comply with the safeguards under Section 35(1)(b) of the BNSS, including recording the reasons showing the necessity of arrest. The record does not disclose satisfactory compliance with the said requirement,” the court said.The court further made it clear that a need to investigate cannot alone justify an arrest.“The mere requirement of further investigation cannot, by itself, justify arrest and detention without following the statutory safeguards,” the court observed.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: Actress Nancy Jennifer, fondly remembered as Bhuvana from Vijay's blockbuster 'Ghilli', has entered a new phase of her personal life.
articles.body: Actress Nancy Jennifer, fondly remembered as Bhuvana from Vijay's blockbuster 'Ghilli', has entered a new phase of her personal life. The actress married Karthik in a traditional wedding ceremony on Sunday, November 15. Pictures and videos from the celebrations have circulated on social media, drawing attention from Tamil cinema fans. Though she had left movies, she was still adored by her fans because of her characters she played as a kid. Her wedding has now brought her back into the spotlight, with fans and well-wishers congratulating the couple.Nancy Jennifer's 'Ghilli' role as Vijay's sister Bhuvana made her popularNancy Jennifer first appeared as a child artiste in the 1997 film 'Nerukku Ner', featuring Vijay and Suriya. She also appeared in films such as 'Thayagam' and 'Ulavu Thurai' alongside Vijayakanth. Nevertheless, the character of Bhuvana in Dharani's 'Ghilli' as Vijay's younger sister made her very popular amongst Tamil moviegoers. The loving name 'Arisimootai' that Vijay gave her character was very well loved by fans.Nancy Jennifer's wedding videos show traditional Hindu marriage ritualsThe marriage took place at a beach resort on Chennai's East Coast Road in a traditional Hindu marriage ceremony. Videos of Karthik tying the mangalsutra around Nancy's neck have gone viral on social media. Their wedding also caught attention because Nancy is a Christian, while Karthik is a Hindu. The actress participated in the Hindu marriage ceremonies, and the visuals sparked discussion. Several social media posts congratulate the couple.Nancy Jennifer's career after 'Ghilli' and her business journeyAfter 'Ghilli', Nancy Jennifer acted in films like 'February 14', 'Unakkum Enakkum', 'Jambhavan', 'Thozha', 'Theeya Velai Seiyyanum Kumaru', 'Koottathil Oruthan' and 'Trip'. She even ventured into television but eventually left acting.In recent times, she has been involved in entrepreneurship through her business venture called Nature's Joy, which produces chemical-free products. articles.title: Ram Gopal Varma backs Namit Malhotra's strategy for 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' and predicts: 'Ramayana 2 will do 10 times more than Ramayana Part 1'
articles.summary: Filmmaker Ram Gopal Varma has once again praised ‘Ramayana: Rise of a Legend’, and this time he has also defended the money plan of producer Namit
articles.body: Filmmaker Ram Gopal Varma has once again praised ‘Ramayana: Rise of a Legend’, and this time he has also defended the money plan of producer Namit Malhotra. In a long post on X, RGV said the film’s theatrical run is so strong that the first part alone may cover the cost of both instalments. He also predicted that the sequel will perform far better.Ram Gopal Varma shares a story about his motherRam Gopal Varma opened his post with a personal story. He said his mother never showed this kind of excitement even for his best films. He wrote, “Even for the best of my films, she didn’t do this, but my mother has been buying tickets for Namit Malhotra’s Ramayana for the servants, watchmen and others in the building complex where she lives.”According to RGV, this wave of excitement has helped the film break records. He believes it is moving towards becoming the “biggest hit ever in Indian cinematic history”. He has watched the film twice and had earlier called it the “Taj Mahal of cinema”.Ram Gopal Varma rejects the Rs 4,000 crore budget claimRam Gopal Varma said some people still argue that the film’s earnings are not enough. Their reasoning is that each of the two parts reportedly cost Rs 2,000 crore, which makes the total Rs 4,000 crore.The filmmaker does not agree with this figure. He claimed that the first part cost slightly less than Rs 800 crore. In his view, this amount already includes mutually beneficial deals, global tax benefits and subsidies, which will bring the cost down even further. He added that any reasonably experienced filmmaker can tell from watching the film that the cost could not have gone beyond this level.He also questioned the idea that both parts would need the same budget. He compared the two films to the two halves of one movie and wrote, “That’s like thinking the cost before the interval and after the interval will be the same in a film. I know of films where 50 per cent of the cost was just the climax.”Why does Ram Gopal Varma talk about ‘Pushpak vimaan’Ram Gopal Varma explained that a large share of the spending went into building the world of ‘Ramayana’. He said these creations will turn into assets that can be used again for the second film, gaming and other projects planned by Malhotra.According to him, most Bollywood filmmakers, trade analysts and self-styled experts do not understand this approach. Based on the current run, he predicted that the producer will get back the full cost of the first part, and possibly of both films, from the first instalment. After that, the earnings from digital and other non-theatrical rights of the first film, along with everything the sequel makes, would be added.Using an image from the epic, RGV joked that Namit Malhotra could then “build his own Pushpak vimaan”. He said the producer could invest in bold ventures that even the biggest production houses in north and south India have not tried. In time, he said, this could even help the producer overtake major Hollywood studios.RGV also took the names of Valmiki and Tulsidas while making a big claim about the producer. He wrote, “I don’t know what happened to Valmiki ji or Tulsidas ji after they did their work, but it is an irrefutable fact that, from now onwards, Namit Malhotra will be the biggest mega filmmaker in history since the May 3, 1913, release of Raja Harishchandra, up to whichever was the biggest film before November 5. If anyone has a doubt, just do the maths.”Why does he expect a bigger part 2The filmmaker said the second part will feature some of the story’s biggest moments. These include action scenes with Hanuman and the Vaanar Sena, Ram Sethu, the burning of Lanka, Sita in Lanka, the death of Kumbhakarna and the killing of Ravana.Ram Gopal Varma said Malhotra has shown a strong mix of strategy, business sense, creative understanding and vision. He compared the two ‘Ramayana’ films with the ‘KGF’ franchise and wrote, “If KGF 2 did around five times more than KGF 1, I am convinced that Ramayana 2 will do 10 times more than Ramayana Part 1. If you disagree, we will talk in 2028.”Second viewing adds to his praiseRam Gopal Varma had earlier said that he was just as impressed after seeing the film a second time. He described himself as an atheist and said he was judging the film as a lover of cinema, not as a devotee of Lord Ram.He praised the scale, ambition, visual effects and performances. In his opinion, some critics failed to see how the grand visuals add to the emotional effect of the story. He gave credit to director Nitesh Tiwari and producer Namit Malhotra for trying something Indian cinema had never imagined before.This is not the first time he has backed the film. In an earlier post, he called it a powerful cinematic experience and asked the makers not to feel low because of poor reviews. He compared the criticism to “barking street dogs” when set against the effort that went into making the film.About the film and its castThe film is produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios along with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations. Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi plays Sita, Yash plays Ravana and Ravie Dubey plays Lakshman. Sunny Deol will be seen as Lord Hanuman, who was introduced in the post-credits scene of the first part. Malhotra and Yash are also co-producers. The second part is expected to arrive on Diwali 2028.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: HBO revela en exclusiva una de las escenas de la serie de ‘Harry Potter’ más míticas de Hogwarts: cuenta con un detalle que no aparece en el libro
articles.standfirst: Un nuevo adelanto deja ver cómo será uno de los momentos más esperados del primer año de Harry
articles.summary: Un nuevo adelanto deja ver cómo será uno de los momentos más esperados del primer año de Harry
articles.body: No hace falta una Snitch dorada para atrapar la atención de los fans: a HBO le ha bastado un puñado de segundos. La serie de Harry Potter ha desvelado en exclusiva una de las escenas más queridas del primer libro, y lo ha hecho con un pequeño giro que ni los lectores más fieles de la saga esperaban. A falta de unas semanas para el estreno, la magia ya ha empezado a hacer efecto. El fragmento, compartido el sábado 14 de noviembre en la cuenta oficial de Harry Potter en Instagram, traslada al espectador al corazón de Hogwarts: el Gran Comedor durante el banquete de bienvenida. Tras la Ceremonia de Selección, los alumnos corean el nombre de Dumbledore y, como por arte de magia, las largas mesas se llenan de carne asada, verduras y postres dignos de Honeydukes. El decorado, levantado desde cero, recuerda mucho al de las películas, con sus mesas de madera, su luz cálida y sus muros de piedra. La auténtica sorpresa está en la mesa de los profesores. El Dumbledore de John Lithgow y la McGonagall de Janet McTeer mantienen una conversación que no aparece en la novela de J.K. Rowling, en la que la profesora comenta cuánto se parece Harry a su padre. Como el libro narra el banquete desde los ojos de Harry, este añadido abre una ventana a lo que piensan los adultos del castillo. El clip, además, funciona como un contrahechizo para las críticas: en el tráiler de septiembre, Harry y Ron aparecían ante un desayuno mucho más modesto, y algunos fans bromearon con la inflación en Hogwarts. Nada más publicarse el clip, las redes sociales se convirtieron en un auténtico Gran Comedor de opiniones, y muchos fans no tardaron en ponerlo frente a frente con la escena original de la película. Hubo quien elogió lo fiel que es la recreación del castillo y su ambiente, y quien celebró ver por fin conversaciones entre los profesores que las películas nunca mostraron. Si bien, las comparaciones siguen siendo odiosas. Hay quienes, han resaltado la falta de color y luz en esta escena mítica.

articles.title: Inside Anirudh Ravichander’s Chennai Home: From bedroom without a bed to memories with Kavya Maran
articles.summary: 'Jailer 2' composer Anirudh Ravichander has achieved fame in Indian film industry due to his popularity with hit songs and film albums.
articles.body: 'Jailer 2' composer Anirudh Ravichander has achieved fame in Indian film industry due to his popularity with hit songs and film albums. However, in his private life, the Chennai house of Anirudh reveals his simplicity and choice. The interior design of the house includes traditional South Indian designs combined with modern interiors. Interestingly, despite his success, Anirudh continues to live with his parents and sister in the family home where he grew up. He had earlier given a tour of the house as part of a painting service's promotion.Inside Anirudh’s house: Traditional entrance and stylish living roomAccording to Indulgexpress, the house features a beautifully carved wooden entrance that gives it a traditional look. The living and dining areas follow an open layout, with a wooden swing placed at the centre. The spacious house has large glass windows that allow sunlight to enter and provide scenic views of the garden outside, which includes mango trees. The living room has white flooring, dark green sofas, and black-and-white chequered chairs. Paintings, decorative pieces and brass idols add to the interiors without making the space look crowded.Anirudh’s memory wall features pictures with Rajinikanth and AR RahmanOne of the special corners in the house is Anirudh’s memory wall, which features photographs from different stages of his life. The composer had described it as a 'before and after' concept. Pictures with his family and popular personalities, including Superstar Rajinikanth and music legend AR Rahman, are also part of the collection. Two chequered chairs placed nearby make it his favourite spot at home. Anirudh had jokingly said that sitting there makes him feel like the 'boss of the house'. The dining area has a glass-top table with six wooden chairs.Home theatre and library added after 'Why This Kolaveri Di' successAnirudh’s family expanded the house after the success of his breakout song 'Why This Kolaveri Di'. They purchased the apartment next door and combined it with their existing home. The additional space now houses a small library and a modern home theatre. Apart from watching films, Anirudh uses the theatre to listen to stories and scripts narrated by directors. A bright yellow sofa adds colour to the otherwise simple interiors.Anirudh’s bedroom has no conventional bedThe composer's bedroom is another interesting part of the house. Unlike most celebrity bedrooms, his room does not have a conventional bed. In contrast, Anirudh likes to sleep on a huge mattress lying directly on the floor. The bedroom has basic furniture, which consists of a recliner, a small table, pictures, and a display for his favorite caps. He had previously said that he doesn’t have many clothes and hence, does not require big wardrobes. With his marriage to Kavya Maran, his Chennai residence continues to be an embodiment of his family values and simple lifestyle.DISCLAIMER: Figures presented in this article are derived from various public sources and are considered approximate unless explicitly noted. articles.title: Jen Affleck says moving to California was meant to bring a 'fresh start' for her and Zac Affleck, but it 'only caused more issues'
articles.summary: In a candid interview, Jen Affleck discusses the challenges of her marriage to Zac Affleck and how a move to California intended for a 'fresh start' led to more issues, ultimately resulting in her filing for divorce amidst an unplanned pregnancy.
articles.body: Jen Affleck figured a move to California might help her and Zac Affleck get the marriage back on track. They'd already been through plenty, and she hoped starting somewhere new would make things easier. It didn't. The problems followed them, and Jen ended up questioning the whole marriage while also dealing with an unplanned pregnancy.She talked about it in season one of 'The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County.' She was pretty upfront about how far things had fallen from what she'd hoped for.Why did Jen and Zac Affleck move to California?Jen and Zac Affleck left Utah for California with their three kids while she explored opportunities in entertainment. She thought the change might let them leave some of their marital problems behind. It didn't make much difference. On the show she said, "I thought moving to California that it could be a chance for Zac and I to really have a fresh start, but it's only caused more issues."None of this would surprise anyone who's watched the earlier seasons. They showed arguments over Zac's gambling, Jen's career ambitions and the strain of having their private lives picked over on TV. They'd even separated briefly before deciding to try again.Jen Affleck opens up about feeling differently during her fourth pregnancyJen Affleck was also pregnant with their fourth child, and she admitted she wasn't feeling the excitement she'd normally expect. Her marriage was already weighing on her, so looking forward to another baby was hard. "When it comes to pregnancy, you should be feeling excitement and anticipation, and I feel bad, but I don't feel those things," she said.She compared it to her pregnancy with Penelope. She'd been questioning the marriage back then too, but having her daughter changed her mind about giving it another shot. "When I got pregnant with Penny, I was definitely questioning my marriage to Zac, but I think having Penny convinced me that it was worth trying again," she explained. This time it wasn't the same. "But that's not happening this time," she added.Jen Affleck files for divorce from Zac after seven years of marriageOn 3 November 2026, Jen Affleck filed for divorce after seven years of marriage. People reported it after getting the court documents from the Fourth Judicial District Court in Provo, Utah. She was pregnant with the fourth baby when she filed. They already have Nora, five, Luca, three, and Penelope, 16 months.People wondered whether Zac Affleck knew it was coming. In an interview with Swooon on 5 November 2026, Jen said he did, and had for ages. "No, he's known for a really long time. We started talking about this a year ago," she said.Zac told his side in a TikTok on 5 November. He said Jen raised concerns about the marriage after she appeared on Dancing With the Stars in 2025. "I basically begged her to stay," he said.What has Jen Affleck said about her relationship with Zac?Jen Affleck had talked about their struggles before filing. In August 2026, she told People they were dealing with several personal issues, and that she was going through prenatal depression and medical problems in her first trimester. She said Zac stepped up when she couldn't cope with the kids. "I could not be there for my kids, and so Zac really had to show up," she told the publication.Zac Affleck spoke to People after the filing too. He said he would "always be Jen's supporter," adding, "Hope she is happy in this next phase of life." He said he was focusing on the kids and working out what comes next for him.The California move was supposed to help. Instead, Jen was left asking whether she wanted to stay in the marriage at all.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Sammy Kershaw accepts CMA apology after country stars speak out over red carpet access
articles.summary: Sammy Kershaw's CMA Awards red carpet denial ignited a firestorm among country music artists who say the industry sidelines legends for influencers.
articles.body: Sammy Kershaw and Rodney Atkins spoke out about being denied permission to walk the red carpet at this year’s Country Music Association Awards, prompting criticism over how the organization treats veteran country artists. Last week, Kershaw, 68, shared a statement on Instagram in which he revealed that the organization rejected his request to walk the carpet at the upcoming ceremony with his wife, Mendy, a decision that he called "extremely hurtful, embarrassing and very disappointing." Following Kershaw's post, Atkins, 57, announced that he and his wife, Rose Falcon, were also denied red carpet access and would no longer be attending the ceremony, which will be held on Nov. 18 and marks the CMAs' milestone 60th anniversary. COUNTRY STAR CODY JOHNSON SAYS NASHVILLE WANTED TO CHANGE HIM BEFORE SUCCESS After facing backlash from other country musicians and fans, the CMA issued a response in which the organization explained that its red carpet criteria helps manage limited space and security needs and apologized to those who "felt excluded by those decisions." The CMA also added that it was speaking with Kershaw's team. On Tuesday, Kershaw shared a post in which he said that he had accepted an apology from the CMA as well as an invitation for himself and Mendy to walk the red carpet and attend the ceremony. The controversy sparked an uproar among country artists, who argued that the CMA has welcomed influencers, actors and crossover celebrities onto the red carpet while sidelining veteran performers. In addition, other country musicians raised broader concerns about how the industry as a whole recognizes artists who helped shape the genre. In his initial post on Nov. 5, Kershaw wrote that the denial of his request to walk the CMAs carpet "really hurts me." He explained that he learned of the rejection just two weeks ahead of the awards show after he and Mendy had already rearranged his touring schedule and booked flights and hotels. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "My wife, Mendy, and I don't get to attend these events very often, due to touring and schedule conflicts," Kershaw wrote at the time. "She was really looking forward to us sharing a special evening together celebrating country music. Then, to find out I was denied the red carpet two weeks before the show, after being strung along for several months and expecting we would be attending, WTF?" Kershaw pointed to his decades-long career and longstanding relationship with the CMA to question why he was excluded. He cited his more than 50 years in the music business, millions of records sold, over two dozen Billboard hits, a past CMA Horizon Award nomination and his status as a "lifetime CMA member" since 1992. The musician also noted that he previously "donated" his time to perform at CMA Fest, and that he hoped he had earned the right to walk the carpet alongside his wife just as they had in the past. "I’m blessed to still be out on tour every year, performing for the greatest fans in the world doing what I love," Kershaw wrote. "I believe there should be room to recognize the artists who have spent their lives contributing to this organization’s success. "I love country music, but never in a million years would I think that a successful country music entertainer (and I’m not the only one) would not be able to walk the red carpet. It’s extremely hurtful, embarrassing and very disappointing. I guess the next time I attend the CMA’s, it will be in tribute after I’m gone, if I’m lucky," he concluded. Two days after Kershaw's post, Atkins shared a video in which he revealed that he and his wife, who is also a longtime CMA member, had also been excluded from the CMAs red carpet and decided to skip the event. "Well, I found out that Sammy Kershaw and I have something in common this year. Neither one of us got approved to walk the CMA awards red carpet," he began. "When I heard about Sammy, I thought, 'What a shame. He's a great guy, sweetheart of a dude. Spent his life representing country music.' Then I found out the same thing happened to me," Atkins continued. "And in a way, I get it. I've always been kind of an outsider, maybe a shrub in the landscape of country music." NATALIE MAINES’ ANTI-TRUMP TIRADE, ZACH BRYAN’S FENCE-CLIMBING CLASH FUEL COUNTRY MUSIC’S BIGGEST FEUDS Atkins went on to emphasize that he was having his strongest touring year, that his album "True South" reached the second round of CMA voting for album of the year and that his latest single could extend his chart presence into a third decade. In a statement the musician shared alongside the video, Atkins expressed his gratitude to his fans "who made this career possible." "You've always made me feel welcome in country music, and that's what matters most," he wrote. "After more than 20 years as a CMA member and countless CMA Fests I’ve played for free, Rose and I were denied red carpet clearance, just like Sammy Kershaw. So we’ve decided not to attend this year’s CMA Awards," Atkins shared. "I also believe the artists who helped build the foundation of country music, like Sammy Kershaw, deserve a place in its celebrations." The ""She Don’t Know She’s Beautiful" singer‘s post was met with supportive comments from other country stars, including some from the younger generation that paid tribute to Kershaw for his foundational contributions to the industry. "If you haven’t earned the right to be there then nobody has… disappointing to say the least," Riley Green wrote. Carly Pearce commented, "Many of us wouldn’t be here without artists like you…" Jake Owen declared himself "Team Sammy," while Granger Smith added, "So sad for country music. I grieve for the old CMA." "This is wild! I’ll give you my spot!!," Drew Bainbridge offered. "You paved the way for all of us on that carpet." Other artists questioned why influencers were invited to walk the carpet while Kershaw was denied. "Ugh this makes me sad for country music. Can we please bring back the legends and not influencers?" Kylie Morgan wrote. "They’ll let zero talent influencers walk the red carpet but not Sammy Kershaw? I hate it here," Meghan Patrick commented. Veteran country star Mark Chesnutt reacted to Kershaw's snub by the CMA in a lengthy statement on Facebook in which he criticized the organization, arguing that it prioritizes celebrities from outside the genre over longtime country artists. "So Sammy Kershaw won’t be allowed to walk the red carpet at the big CMA Awards," he wrote. "Well that’s about right. The CMA doesn’t care about us old 90s guys any more." "It’s a shame they don’t respect the stars that dominated the charts in the past thirty years or before that but they sure roll out the welcome mat for pop stars and Hollywood movie stars and even hip hop artists," he continued. "Anything but country music gets the performance spots on the show." Chesnutt also contrasted the country music industry's treatment of the genre’s history with the recognition received by rock icons. "Rock n Roll honors its history and respects its legends while country music industry executives seem to ignore its rich history and its legends," he wrote. "Thank God there’s still a lot of people that love traditional country music. They keep coming to our shows and showing their love and respect for the music we’ve made for nearly forty years now and we’ll keep working for them and not for those who don’t matter to US!" Country singer Pam Tillis, who also rose to fame in the 1990s, also addressed Kershaw's red carpet denial, though she clarified that her criticism was not solely directed at the CMA. "So let’s talk about today’s drama in country music: Sammy Kershaw and the CMAs. I’m not going to single out the CMA, because this happens all the time in our business," she wrote in a post on Instagram. "It’s the nature of our industry that the rising stars get the spotlight, just as we did at one point." Tillis emphasized the importance of preserving a legacy, pointing to her own experience growing up as the daughter of country icon Mel Tillis. "I learned early that a legacy doesn’t keep itself," she wrote. "Somebody has to stand up and say, ‘This artist mattered. They made a contribution.’ I’ve done that for Daddy most of my life." She acknowledged that rising stars naturally receive attention, but argued that established performers still connect with generations of fans. PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE "And I’ll tell you what I’ve seen: the country audience is a multigenerational audience, and ‘90s country is still very viable, even if it isn’t always visible," she wrote. "A lot of us have three generations of fans showing up to our shows, singing, whooping and hollering for our songs. Many of today’s artists are making it big with their own spin on the ‘90s sound." "I dare say many of us have felt the sting of being passed over for this, that and the other, in order to create an image that’s only part of the picture," Tillis continued. "I know today’s new artists need all the support they can get in such a crazy, competitive market. But legacy artists who want to show up can be the bridge between where this music came from and where it’s going." "Many of us never say anything about these slights," she added. "We just keep on doing our thing. As an artist who is a lifetime CMA member, Sammy just spoke out." On Monday, the CMA released a statement responding to the backlash and citing space and security criteria for red carpet management. "In recent days, several artists and their fans have spoken out about this year’s CMA Awards red carpet guidelines," the organization wrote. "Like any major televised event, the red carpet has criteria that exists to help manage limited space and the security needs for both the artists and the media. We are deeply sorry anyone felt excluded by those decisions." "Our organization’s mission is to honor the history and celebrate the excellence of Country Music," it continued. "With this 60th anniversary year, we are working extra hard to simultaneously spotlight the last six decades, while also celebrating what has been a tremendous year in 2026. It’s not easy to do all of that in just one night, but we are up for the challenge." "We also know this is about more than a red carpet, and we are committed to keep listening and keep finding ways to make sure all artists feel welcome and at home here," the CMA added. "To that point, we are in touch with Sammy Kershaw’s team and look forward to continuing that conversation." On Tuesday, Kershaw shared a positive update, revealing that CMA leadership had "extended a sincere, heartfelt apology" which he had accepted following a "sincere and meaningful private conversation." "The CMA has also extended an invitation for my wife, Mendy, and me to walk the red carpet and attend this year's awards alongside our fellow artists," he wrote. "I am grateful for that invitation and appreciate their willingness to listen, acknowledge our concerns, and work toward a positive outcome." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE Kershaw also thanked fans, fellow artists and the country music community for their support. He explained that he originally spoke publicly because he was hurt, rather than seeking attention or controversy. The "Cadillac Style" singer emphasized that the controversy was about more than his personal invitation. "This was never about the red carpet," he wrote. "It was about recognizing and respecting those who dedicated their lives to this music and preserving the history and legacy that makes country music so special." Kershaw expressed his hopes that the conversations would produce lasting change in how legacy artists are recognized. "You cannot celebrate 60 years of country music without celebrating the artists who helped build those 60 years," he wrote. "I have nothing but respect for the incredible talent carrying country music into the future. Every generation of artists deserves its moment to shine, and I believe there’s room to celebrate all of them."

articles.title: Soni Razdan recalls smoking 100 cigarettes a day when she was pregnant with Alia Bhatt, during 'Gumraah' shoot: 'I had no clue, I'm not a smoker'
articles.summary: Alia Bhatt continued working throughout her pregnancy in 2022, even performing action sequences for her Hollywood debut, Tom Harper’s Netflix thriller
articles.body: Alia Bhatt continued working throughout her pregnancy in 2022, even performing action sequences for her Hollywood debut, Tom Harper’s Netflix thriller 'Heart of Stone'. She also stepped into production with Jasmeet K Reen’s dark comedy thriller 'Darlings', which released just three months before she welcomed daughter Raha Kapoor. However, Alia seems to have inherited her work ethic from her mother, Soni Razdan, who continued shooting during both her pregnancies in the late 1980s and early 1990s.Soni recalled discovering her first pregnancy while filming for the television show 'Buniyaad'. The Ramesh Sippy and Jyoti Swarup-directed series marked her television debut in 1986 and ran until 1987.“I got pregnant first while shooting for Buniyaad,” Soni recalled. She also spoke about the support she received from the show's makers during that period, particularly when travelling to the sets was a challenge. “The Sippys were so good to me. I was living in the boonies in the Lokhandwala complex, where you used to not even get a taxi in the morning to go to a shoot. We’d just started as a married couple. I didn’t have a car. They’d send me a car so that I didn’t have the stress of finding transport at 6 am. At that time, Lokhandwala wasn’t developed at all. Even on set, they gave me the best room and took good care of me,” she said in an interview with Screen.After welcoming her first daughter, Shaheen Bhatt, with filmmaker Mahesh Bhatt in 1988, Soni became pregnant again while shooting for her husband's 1993 crime thriller 'Gumrah'. Recalling one particularly unusual experience from the shoot, she revealed that she had no idea she was expecting Alia at the time.“I was shooting that smoking scene, and I’d have smoked some 100 cigarettes in one day. I had no clue Alia was inside me! I’m not a smoker, but after that, I was just craving cigarettes,” revealed Soni, laughing.She also performed the film's much-discussed gallows sequence while pregnant. However, when she returned to the sets after a five-month break, her pregnancy had begun to show, creating a challenge with her costumes.“I also did that famous gallows scene when I was pregnant with her. Then there was a big break. Five months later, when I came back, my costumes wouldn’t fit me. I had a little bump by then. So, we had to alter the costumes,” she added.Soni pointed out that the film industry has become considerably more accommodating towards working mothers over the years. She is particularly happy that Alia does not have to conceal her motherhood or treat it as something that could affect her professional commitments.“It’s changed a lot. Nowadays, the mindset is completely different for producers, directors, and actors, which is so important. I’m so gratified by the fact that Alia doesn’t have to pretend she’s not a mom. Because at that time, we had to tiptoe around the fact that we had children so that the producer wouldn’t get stressed that I’d have to run away if my child fell sick,” said Soni.The actor also recounted an incident from the time she was shooting for Mahesh Bhatt's 1995 television show 'A Mouthful of Sky' in Mumbai's Saki Naka. A paging call informed her that both her daughters, Shaheen and Alia, had been locked out of their house. Shaheen was seven at the time, while Alia was only three.“I remember I had such trauma on set trying to figure out how to get my children back into the house or into the neighbour’s house because they were on the steps. Those days are thankfully over, and actresses can be freely pregnant while they’re shooting. I never took any break. The break took me,” she added, laughing.Soni also credited Cinevistaas Limited for providing her with consistent work during those years, particularly when being married to Mahesh Bhatt became a reason for some people in the industry to assume she no longer needed professional opportunities. The production house backed her with projects such as A Salam's 'Junoon', which aired from 1994 to 1998, and Surendra Mohan's family drama 'Saahil', which ran from 1995 to 1996.“Cinevistaas actually rescued me, I’d say. I was newly married, and people said, ‘Why does she need to work now? She’s Mahesh Bhatt’s wife.’ So, they used to not give me work.”She specifically remembered the supportive attitude of Cinevistaas chairperson Prem Kishen Malhotra and managing director Sunil Mehta, who were willing to offer her opportunities without making assumptions about her personal life.“My agent went up to them, and they said, ‘Yes, of course!’ They were the sweetest people to work with. Even before we started shooting, they said, ‘You want money? We’ll give you money in advance.’ I said, ‘No no, I just want to work’ (laughs). They were like a family, and ensured I had work and was working at least 10 days a month,” said Soni.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
