articles.title: Johnny Depp fled Hollywood spotlight for quiet Bahamas life where 'nobody’s pointing a camera at me'
articles.summary: Johnny Depp opens up about how his 1940s Bahamas wood house with a yurt and painting studio became his sanctuary away from cameras and fame.
articles.body: Johnny Depp turns to the Bahamas to experience a private life. During an interview with the Wall Street Journal, Depp opened up about craving privacy and not being able to have it in the United States. "Today, I live most of the time in the Bahamas. It’s where I’ve found total peace and quiet. Nobody’s pointing a camera at me or staring. I bought my 1940s wood house in 2004 and added a yurt and a painting studio. Art continues to be a sanctuary that lets me process the world around me," Depp told the outlet. ‘GREASE’ STAR STOCKARD CHANNING SAYS SHE’S ‘HAPPY BEING A RECLUSE’ AFTER LEAVING AMERICA Depp famously purchased his own island in the Bahamas in 2004. In 2009, he told Vanity Fair that "escapism is survival to me," and that, after playing a difficult role, "my head was done in. I needed to escape. So being able to get on the boat and move allowed my head freedom again." He continued, "Somehow, the mathematics led me here to my island. I don’t think I’d ever seen any place so pure and beautiful. You can feel your pulse rate drop about 20 beats. It’s instant freedom. And that rare beast—simplicity—can be had. And a little morsel of anonymity." The actor added, "Whenever I was getting frustrated about being ‘novelty boy’ and making movies, I told myself, Calm down. I can come down here and disappear." Depp told SCMP Style in 2023, "Where I feel the most myself in this world, and where I go to feel absolutely normal, I suppose, is my place in the Bahamas, because it’s an island and nobody’s looking at me. You’ve got to have some sanctuary, a safe place where you can escape the scrutiny and the interest of others, a place where you can just sit on a beach, read, paint, meditate or whatever, that’s freedom to me. That’s the only real freedom." Making music is also something Depp likes to do on his island. Telling WSJ about how he passes his time there, he said, "I like to grab about four or five books and flop on the couch and read. Or I play guitar in my music studio." In the 80s, Depp was in a band – music was what originally brought him to Los Angeles in 1983, not acting. "Soon after, I met actor Nicolas Cage at a friend’s house. Nic came to see my band several times, and we became friends," Depp said. "Six months later, he suggested I try acting. I was up for anything that would help pay the bills." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? Depp stars as the title role in "Ebenezer," which debuted on Friday. Speaking to "CBS Mornings," Depp discussed the movie and the impact his children have had on his career. "There was a great veil lifted when my first child was born. And suddenly, I understood exactly what everything had been for," Depp said. "There were years of that, that I thought, ‘What am I doing? articles.title: Richard Sterban of The Oak Ridge Boys dead at 83
articles.summary: Richard Sterban's iconic bass voice powered The Oak Ridge Boys' "Elvira" to No. 1. His family revealed he battled pancreatic cancer since March.
articles.body: Richard Sterban, whose unmistakable voice helped make The Oak Ridge Boys’ "Elvira" a country music classic, has died. He was 83. The singer died Saturday, Nov. 14, in Hendersonville, Tennessee, from complications of bronchitis and pneumonia following a long battle with cancer, according to an announcement from his family and The Oak Ridge Boys. "We appreciate all of your love, support, and prayers. Please continue to lift us up in this difficult time, we find comfort knowing that he is currently face to face with Jesus," his family said in a statement obtained by Fox News Digital. Sterban publicly announced his pancreatic cancer diagnosis in September 2025, revealing that doctors had diagnosed him that March. Despite his health struggles, the country music veteran expressed hope that his faith and medical care would help him recover and return to performing. JOHN ANDERSON, COUNTRY MUSIC HALL OF FAMER, DEAD AT 71 "With the help of the Good Lord above, I believe I will be able to get through this," he said at the time. He also thanked fans for their prayers and said he hoped to return to the road within several months. NEW PANCREATIC CANCER PILL COULD RESHAPE TREATMENT AS EARLY TRIAL RESULTS STUN RESEARCHERS After stepping away from touring in May 2025, Sterban returned to the Grand Ole Opry on Jan. 30 and 31, 2026, joining his bandmates for performances of "Elvira" that brought audiences to their feet, according to the announcement. "Having Richard on stage with us again was one of God’s greatest blessings," fellow Oak Ridge Boys singer Duane Allen said. GEORGE STRAIT PULLS OFF INCREDIBLE CAREER ACCOMPLISHMENT WITH STUNNING CONCERT Born April 24, 1943, in Camden, New Jersey, Sterban began singing in Sunday school at age 6. His voice transitioned from soprano to bass by eighth grade, setting him on a path that would eventually take him from gospel quartets to some of music’s biggest stages. Before joining The Oak Ridge Boys, Sterban performed behind Elvis Presley as a member of J.D. Sumner and the Stamps Quartet. He toured and recorded with Presley and appeared in the 1972 concert film, "Elvis on Tour." Later that year, he left the job to become The Oak Ridge Boys’ bass singer. "I wanted to be in the best vocal group in the world," Sterban said, according to the announcement. Alongside lead singer Allen, baritone William Lee Golden and tenor Joe Bonsall, Sterban helped transform the Southern gospel quartet into a country and pop crossover act. Their hits included "Y’all Come Back Saloon," "Bobbie Sue," and "American Made." But it was Sterban’s booming bass refrain on the group’s 1981 recording of "Elvira" that became his musical calling card. The song reached No. 1 on the country chart and No. 5 on the pop chart and earned a Grammy Award. OUTLAW COUNTRY SINGER DAVID ALLAN COE DEAD AT 86 "It’s the song everyone hopes to hear at our concerts," Sterban said on its 40th anniversary, according to the announcement. The group became Grand Ole Opry members in 2011 and entered the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2015. DOLLY PARTON DEAD AT 80 Their decades together also forged deep personal bonds. In January 2021, Allen reflected on his relationship with Sterban, Golden and Bonsall. "I think the four of us have grown closer than we’ve ever been in our whole career," Allen told Fox News Digital at the time. RANDY TRAVIS’ WIFE SAYS DOCTORS GAVE COUNTRY LEGEND 1% CHANCE OF SURVIVAL BEFORE MIRACULOUS COMEBACK The Oak Ridge Boys also developed a lasting friendship with former President George H.W. Bush. At his request, they performed "Amazing Grace" at his funeral in Houston in December 2018, taking an overnight flight after a concert in Washington state to attend. "There’s no way we wouldn’t do it," Sterban said, according to the announcement. Away from the stage, Sterban was a devoted baseball fan and a part owner of the Nashville Sounds minor league team for 30 years. He continued recording late in life, contributing to several tracks on The Oak Ridge Boys’ October 2026 album, "Buried Treasures." articles.title: ‘Haven’t heard the last of me’: Tearful Phil Collins makes emotional speech at Rock & Roll Hall of Fame ceremony
articles.summary: Phil Collins gave a tearful acceptance speech and got an electrifying tribute from Cynthia Erivo, Oprah Winfrey inducted the late Luther Vandross, the crowd yelled along with Billy Idol, and Wu-Tang Clan crowded the stage for a rowdy celebration at the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony on Saturday night.
articles.body: LOS ANGELES — Phil Collins gave a tearful acceptance speech and got an electrifying tribute from Cynthia Erivo, Oprah Winfrey inducted the late Luther Vandross, the crowd yelled along with Billy Idol, and Wu-Tang Clan crowded the stage for a rowdy celebration at the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony on Saturday night. Queen Latifah, Oasis, MC Lyte, Sade, Joy Division/New Order and Iron Maiden were also inducted at the ceremony at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles along with producer Rick Rubin, who got a long-bearded tribute from the Red Hot Chili Peppers. A night that beforehand felt like it might fall flat with the absences of key inductees was as lively and overloaded as the induction ceremony ever is. U2 was the night’s surprise opener, playing their new single “Silencio” while surrounded by dancers in riot squad gear. They then launched into their 1984 classic “Pride (In the Name of Love)” as singer Bono alternately raised a peace sign and fist. Run DMC and Aerosmith were the surprise closers with a loud jam of “Walk This Way,” their 1986 classic collaboration, produced by Rubin, that brought the merger of rock and rap to a new level. Collins gets emotional, Idol gets wild The 75-year-old Collins, whose mobility trouble and other health problems kept him from performing, took the stage slowly using a pair of canes and cried at a huge ovation from a crowd that included his daughter, actor Lily Collins, and four other children. Blink-182 drummer Travis Barker inducted Collins and praised him for his unprecedented dual stardom as a drummer and a hit-making pop singer in the 1980s. “I grew up just wanting to play the drums,” Collins said. “Everything else has been a really happy accident. I can’t believe, when I look back, how life has gone.” Barker said Collins’ song “In the Air Tonight” gave the world “arguably the most badass drum fill of all time.” Minutes later, Barker played that drum fill himself as Erivo gave a slowed-down, epic rendition of the song with a wailing crescendo that brought the crowd to its feet. Collins was already in the hall as a member of Genesis, but now gets the solo honor. He hasn’t been able to take the stage since 2022, but assured the crowd that “you haven’t heard the last of me.” Hours later, the crowd leapt to its feet and shouted along with “White Wedding” during the induction of Idol — one of the few artists ticket buyers knew for sure would show up and perform. He was inducted along with his longtime guitarist Steve Stevens by No Doubt members Tony Kanal and Gwen Stefani, who joined Idol for a duet on “Eyes Without a Face.” “I say to all the young people out there who can barely tune a guitar and work a sampler, ‘Now it’s your turn,’” Idol said. He ended with, “And now, I’m gonna party with the Wu-Tang Clan!” Oprah inducts Luther Vandross Winfrey said with relish that Vandross was “the maestro of the love song” and said he was once correctly named “the top artist that people make looove to.” Vandross, an R&B singer with a velvet voice, was one of the definitive singers of the 1980s and ’90s. He died in 2005. “Luther Vandross sang with such passion and soul it could reach something deep inside that you didn’t even know needed to be reached,” Winfrey said. Usher then took the stage and sang a sultry medley of Vandross hits, including “Here and Now” and “So Amazing.” Hip-hop acts make their presence known Wu-Tang Clan, the epic hip-hop collective from New York’s Staten Island, filled the stage with its 10 current members, giving a memorable acceptance speech and a performance that had the crowd on its feet dancing. Backed by a big jazz band, the musical medley included “C.R.E.A.M.,” “Method Man” and late member Ol’ Dirty Bastard’s “Shimmy Shimmy Ya.” “Wu-Tang rewrote the rules of hip-hop and did it without a big machine behind them,” said comedian Chris Rock, who inducted them. “We took Staten Island to the world,” the group’s leader RZA said. “We had a desire to conquer.” He added, “We wanted to make a mark. We made our mark.” MC Lyte, a trailblazing female rapper starting in the late 1980s, was the first artist inducted, with hip-hop star Remy Ma doing the honors and calling her “one of the first women in hip-hop to make sure there was room for the rest of us.” MC Lyte said she was a “B-girl from Brooklyn just looking for my chance to inspire and motivate.” Her contemporary and fellow groundbreaker Latifah was inducted later in the evening by Megan Thee Stallion, who said Latifah “taught us to recognize royalty within ourselves.” Latifah said that for a long time, she would not have believed this night was possible. “It’s difficult enough being a woman in hip-hop,” she said, “let alone being a hip-hopper in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame.” Latifah and MC Lyte then took the stage together to perform a medley of their hits, including Latifah’s “U.N.I.T.Y.” and MC Lyte’s “Ruffneck.” They entered the hall as recipients of the Early Influence Award along with posthumous inductees Gram Parsons, Fela Kuti and Celia Cruz, who were all inducted via video tribute. A stage full of Rick Rubins Legendary rock, hip-hop and country producer Rubin accepted his induction with a one-sentence acceptance speech. “You can’t kill rock ‘n’ roll,” he said, and left the stage. The Red Hot Chili Peppers then appeared, all four of them wearing white wigs and long white fake beards to match Rubin’s signature look as they played their 1991 breakthrough hit “Give It Away,” one of many he produced for them. Longtime Hall-of-Famer Neil Young inducted Rubin, making fun of his tendency to work while lying barefoot on the couch and praising him for the unmatched care he takes with his artists, including the Beastie Boys, Run DMC, Johnny Cash, the Chicks and Adele. Oasis and the other no-shows Oasis, the youngest of the inductees, didn’t show up. Guitarist Noel Gallagher was playing a gig back home in Britain, and his little brother, Liam Gallagher, just didn’t want to come. “Anybody surprised they didn’t show up?” asked actor and Oasis superfan Bob Odenkirk, who inducted them. “It would’ve been out of character if they had. I would’ve been worried.” Stephen Wilson Jr. gave an acoustic rendition of their biggest hit “Wonderwall.” Iron Maiden, the quintessential British heavy metal band of the 1980s, opted to stay on tour in Australia. “They aren’t even here tonight, because they’re rocking a world tour, as they have done for the last 50 years!” said actor Jack Black during their induction. A supergroup featuring members of Metallica, Rage Against the Machine and St. Vincent then played “The Trooper” in tribute. Joy Division, a dark and seminal post-punk band, and New Order, which was formed by its members after singer Ian Curtis died in 1980, got a joint induction. Trent Reznor of Nine Inch Nails inducted them, saying Joy Division’s members were “the authors of an unbreakable archetype.” Only the bassist for both bands, Peter Hook, appeared at the ceremony. He performed Joy Division’s “Love Will Tear Us Apart” and New Order’s “Bizarre Love Triangle” with Deftones and singer Lauren Mayberry of the band Chvrches. Hook said the young musicians “made an old man very happy.” He has had long-running feuds with his fellow bandmates and, other than Curtis, didn’t mention any of them in his acceptance speech. Sade also decided to skip the induction. The singer and her band that’s named after her were inducted by singer Andra Day and celebrated by singer Sienna Spiro, who sang the group’s beloved hit “Smooth Operator.” After streaming the ceremony live for the past few years, the Rock Hall returned to its previous format, where the public won’t see it until an edited version airs on ABC and Disney+ on Dec. 9.

articles.title: Could a viral teen comedy be Netflix’s answer to YouTube?
articles.summary: Netflix is hoping Gen Z audiences stream “Minimum Wage,” which began as a web series in 2024.
articles.body: LIVERPOOL, N.Y. — Inside a make-believe pizza shop overlooking Onondaga Lake, a team of digital creators, filmmakers and young actors spent months cooking up a show that they hope will serve Netflix something it craves: a fresh audience. “Minimum Wage,” a mockumentary that follows teens who work at a pizza shop, has garnered more than 30 million views across YouTube, TikTok and Instagram since launching in May 2024. Now, Netflix is betting that Gen Z audiences will watch the viral hit in its expanded form on the streaming giant — and pay to view it. The media company’s decision to acquire the show reflects a broader shift in Hollywood’s battle for younger viewers, as streamers increasingly turn to internet creators and their built-in fan bases to drive subscriptions and engagement. Of course, it’s not a new strategy. For years, the industry has tried to tap into YouTube’s massive roster of creators. Sometimes, it’s a success: Amazon Prime’s reality competition series with YouTuber MrBeast, for example, became the platform’s most streamed unscripted series of all time. Other times, however, it’s more of a bust — like Netflix’s “Haters Back Off,” a comedy series with former YouTube star Colleen Ballinger, aka Miranda Sings, which was canceled after just two seasons. But there has been a noticeable uptick in creator content across streaming in 2026. According to data from London-based market research firm Ampere Analysis, first published in Puck, creator-led programming across 16 U.S. streaming services surged more than 300% in the third quarter of 2026 compared with the same period a year earlier. “YouTube is not just UGC [user-generated content] and cat videos anymore,” Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos said during the 2025 fourth quarter earnings call. “They are TV. So we all compete with them in every dimension for talent, for ad dollars, for subscription dollars and for all forms of content.” With “Minimum Wage,” showrunner writer and executive producer Will Phelps said his agent at UTA “called up all the different streamers, and a couple different streamers wanted it … so we got multiple offers.” He did not disclose which streamers were vying for the show’s rights. But in the end, Phelps said, Netflix emerged as the strongest partner for American High Shorts, the production company behind the project. “We wanted to do it the way we were doing it on YouTube, but just on a bigger scope,” said Phelps, who co-showruns with Jeremy Garelick and Axelle Azoulay. “And rather than pushing us to do something glossy and different, Netflix let us do what we do best,” Phelps added. “Except for now, we have a huge platform.” Phelps, Garelick and Azoulay were able to retain creative control over the writing and directing. And Netflix allowed the original cast of largely unfamiliar faces to stay on — including Grace Reiter, who recently joined “Saturday Night Live.” Comedian Randall Park was also added to the ensemble, playing Terry Sylvester, founder, CEO and franchise owner of the struggling Slice Club pizzeria chain. Episodes are typically between 12 and 20 minutes in length, as opposed to the traditional 30-minute sitcoms that populate network television. Phelps, a veteran of the entertainment industry, said he believes the key to making a quality show is maintaining the elements of a strong story, while tailoring the format to the viewer’s attention span. Recent data from UCLA’s Center for Scholars & Storytellers (CSS), a nonprofit research center, supports his assertion. Nearly 4 in 5 of the 1,500 survey respondents ages 10-24 said short-form videos can tell a story, according to the fifth annual “Teens and Screens” report, which was published in October. While older generations identify storytelling with books, TV and movies, the same boundaries do not exist for younger generations, the report found. “This is the first generation to grow up on video-first platforms, so for them short, creator-driven video simply is television,” Yalda T. Uhls, founder and CEO of CSS, told NBC News in an email. For shows like “Minimum Wage” to succeed on streaming, young audiences have to find it authentic. Thus far, the show has picked up buzz among viewers. The week the show launched, it was in the global top 10 of shows on Netflix, placing sixth behind Season 11 of “Love is Blind.” Critics have also praised it — helping it notch a fresh score of 81% on the Rotten Tomatoes Tomatometer. One reviewer described the series as Gen Z’s version of “The Office,” NBC’s hit mockumentary sitcom that was set at the fictional Dunder Mifflin Paper Company in Scranton, Pennsylvania. “A show like ‘Minimum Wage’ arrives with proof that an audience already loves it,” Uhls said. “The key is to bring over what made it work, meaning the creator’s voice and its authenticity, instead of polishing it into something generic.”

articles.title: Rachelle Hampton won’t admit how long she spent charting the use of ‘murmur’ in Twilight
articles.summary: Normal Gossip host Rachelle Hampton is obsessed with I Like to Watch and splurges on good butter.
articles.body: Rachelle Hampton is a writer and co-owner at Defector Media, and the host of Normal Gossip, a podcast of anonymous listener-submitted stories about everyday drama. Whether that’s lies about luxury wool in a literal knitting circle, the impeachment of a hypocritical HOA president, or a COVID outbreak at a destination wedding with an absurd 25 bridesmaids, each story is unique in its absurdity, yet weirdly relatable. After years as one of the co-hosts of Slate’s In Case You Missed It, a podcast that required her to be chronically online, Hampton is enjoying being a little more unplugged these days. And she has perhaps the most interesting answer we’ve ever received to the question “what’s worth splurging on?” What is your most indispensable tool (analog or digital, app or hardware)? I think it has to be the Notes app. My entire life is in there! My relationship to the Notes app definitely changes depending on what’s going on in my life at the time. Sometimes I just use it to make my grocery lists, but there was also a period of time where I used it to house my weekly to-do list, so it was basically the only thing between me and destruction. I’ve started blog drafts in the Notes app, and I’ve used it to write out particularly fraught text messages. There are recipes I’ve developed in there, as well as passwords and also questions for my doctors. The first note in my phone is from 2018, so it also serves as a nearly decade-long journal, though there are definitely notes that I simply can’t decipher, like why do I have a note from July 2020 that just says “4th floor”? Which is the most underappreciated? I absolutely hate texting. (I write all day, I don’t want to do it in my free time!!) But as someone who also refuses to delete their texts, I have to acknowledge that my most significant personal archive is probably in my Messages inbox. What is the first app you install on a new phone or computer? It’s a tie between Spotify and whatever phone game I’m currently addicted to, which for the last two years has been Township. I’ve never played Sims or Animal Crossing, but I’m told that it’s something like that. I just like planting my little crops. How many tabs do you have open right now? I maintain inbox zero across my entire digital life, so I close all my tabs after I finish a task. Right now I have three tabs that I will close immediately after finishing this questionnaire: the first is the Google Doc I’m typing in, the second is the landing page for this series, and the third is a Google tab where I just searched Animal Crossing to make sure I had the name right. Which social media platform do you use the most? It’s a tie between Reddit and YouTube. Hosting a twice-weekly podcast about the internet for three years either gave me some sort of PTSD or cured me of my social media addiction, depending on how you want to look at it. I can’t spend more than twenty minutes max on IG or X or Bluesky without feeling claustrophobic. The exception is when I’m sick, and I let my fever brain rot on IG reels. Otherwise, it just feels like too much information from too many different sources. Reddit and YouTube are both places where I feel somewhat in control of what I’m seeing. What is your happy place online? I don’t think I’ve ever been as happy online as I was on Tumblr between 2013 and 2016. I’m always subconsciously chasing that high. What is your favorite gadget you’ve ever owned? My older brother bought me a tabletop Klipsch Bluetooth speaker for Christmas a couple of years ago, and it’s still going strong. The sound quality is incredible, and the design is super sexy, so it doesn’t immediately read as a Bluetooth speaker, which I love. I hope I never have to replace it. Which tech trend do you wish would go away? One of the stances I’m proudest of is that I’ve never (intentionally) used ChatGPT or Midjourney or any of the other generative AI tools / large language models. It’s getting harder and harder to avoid now that Gemini is built into Google and its various products. Stop trying to write my emails, Gemini!! I’ve never been swayed away from my belief that every single AI company owes a bankrupting amount of money to the writers and artists whose work their products are built on. Until that debt is paid, there’s nothing appealing to me about talking to a chatbot or creating a shitty poster. What creation are you most proud of? In 2020, when I was a staff writer at Slate, I spent a [redacted amount of time] methodically charting and ranking all 349 times Stephenie Meyer used the word murmur in her iconic Twilight saga. The idea had been germinating somewhere in the recesses of my brain for over a decade, only to be released by the surprise 2020 release of Midnight Sun. Seeing this blog come to life (shout out Slate’s interactive designer Natalie Matthews-Ramo!) felt like a fever dream come true. What is your current obsession? I’ve rewatched every episode of Netflix’s I Like to Watch with drag queens Trixie Mattel and Katya an embarrassing amount of times. There are certain episodes, like this one where Trixie and Katya react to Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery, that I can quote front to back. [Media: What do you do when you’re feeling stuck? I wish I could say something chill and zen like take a cold shower or something, but the truth is when I’m writing and feeling stuck, I usually smoke a little weed, preferably a sativa strain. Getting high gets me out of my own way, which is usually the problem when I’m feeling stuck. It particularly helps with scriptwriting for Normal Gossip because the tone is so conversational, so being a little bit high stops me from over-writing. When was the last time you went somewhere without your phone? articles.summary: Cameron Mathison opens up to Fox News Digital about kidney cancer, divorce, wildfire loss and how those struggles led him to "A Very Arctic Christmas" with Jill Wagner.
articles.body: Cameron Mathison knew something was wrong — and spent two years pushing for answers before an MRI revealed he had cancer. The "General Hospital" star told Fox News Digital the frightening experience changed how he approaches his health, including knowing when to stop pushing his body. 'LIONESS' STAR JILL WAGNER RAISES DAUGHTERS IN TENNESSEE TOWN OF 800, WHERE HORSES AND BUGGIES STILL ROAM Mathison was diagnosed with renal cell carcinoma, a type of kidney cancer, in 2019 after an MRI revealed a tumor. Before his diagnosis, the actor said he had gone to extraordinary lengths to monitor his health, undergoing bloodwork, gut microbiome testing and hormone evaluations. Despite those efforts, he said, troubling results left him searching for an explanation. "I was a guy trying to do it right, but like I was alluding to, I was very extreme," he said. "And I was doing these extreme things, and I was getting the blood tests, and … things were just off … they were like red flags." WATCH: CAMERON MATHISON FOUGHT FOR 2 YEARS TO GET LIFE-SAVING MRI The experience left him with a message for others facing unanswered health questions. articles.title: Johnny Depp’s ‘Ebenezer’ Unwraps $19M to Win Weekend in Box Office Return
articles.summary: Fellow newcomers 'Ghost Soldier' and 'How to Rob a Bank' are getting quieter starts over the weekend.
articles.body:
Ebenezer unwrapped $19 million domestically as star Johnny Depp's studio comeback vehicle opened in first place at the domestic box office.

Paramount Pictures released director Ti West's horror-tinged adaptation of Charles Dickens' A Christmas Carol in 3,535 North American theaters this weekend and landed an A- CinemaScore from audiences. Of the opening Thursday night audience, 62 percent of the crowd was over age 30, suggesting that the film was especially appealing for those who likely have positive associations with seeing Depp's work throughout the decades. Ebenezer earned 4.5 out of 5 stars on PostTrak, with 50 percent of guests citing Depp as their reason for seeing the movie.

It took in $23 million from international markets for a global start of $42 million.

Rupert Grint, Andrea Riseborough, Sam Claflin, Daisy Ridley and Ian McKellen round out the cast for the $38 million-budgeted feature that stars Depp as the miserly Ebenezer Scrooge who is visited by three spirits. Ebenezer marks Depp's first studio project since 2018's Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald , as he took a hiatus from high-profile work following abuse allegations from ex-wife Amber Heard that Depp has denied, in addition to negative headlines amid his and Heard's 2022 defamation trial .

Paramount had been pleased with data suggesting that audiences want Depp back and that he still holds wide appeal, with the marketing including the actor appearing in character as Scrooge to remind fans of other transformative roles like Captain Jack Sparrow and Willy Wonka. Ebenezer has a PG-13 rating but is still geared toward the family crowd. Critics have been split on Ebenezer , as it holds a 53 percent approval rating from Rotten Tomatoes reviewers. In his review for The Hollywood Reporter , critic Frank Scheck declares that the film "fulfills its ostensible goal of restoring the actor to A-list status."

Among other new arrivals, Sony Pictures released Ghost Soldier in 2,558 North American locations on Wednesday, with director William Eubank's action movie grossing around $5.2 million for the three-day frame and a $8.3 million domestic cume. Jim Caviezel plays a former Green Beret who must defend his Wyoming community against a corporate threat. Hailing from Mandalay Pictures, Ghost Soldier holds a 42 percent score from Rotten Tomatoes critics and a 90 percent from audiences.

Not bagging much of a haul is Amazon MGM Studios' How to Rob a Bank , director David Leitch's heist movie, also grossing $5.2 million for the frame. Nicholas Hoult, Zoë Kravitz and Anna Sawai star in the $40 million-budgeted ensemble film about a group of bank robbers who document their exploits on social media. It has taken $10.3 million globally.

How to Rob a Bank is opening well below Leitch's recent work, including 2022's Bullet Train ($30 million domestic debut) and 2024's The Fall Guy ($27.7 million domestic debut), although those featured more proven box office draws in Brad Pitt and Ryan Gosling, respectively. The new movie, which earned a B- CinemaScore, has come up a bit empty with critics. It holds a 33 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and an 80 percent audience score, with THR chief film critic David Rooney noting in his review that "the fun wears a bit thin."

Warner Bros.' The Cat in the Hat is set to pounce on second place in its sophomore frame, grossing roughly $10 million domestically for the weekend to bring its North American sum to $36.7 million for a respectable decline of around 50 percent. Bill Hader voices the titular unpredictable feline in directors Erica Rivinoja and Alessandro Carloni's animated retelling of Dr. Seuss' classic children's book.

Overall, the domestic marketplace collected $90 million for the quiet frame, down 25.9 percent from last weekend, although it was up 18.4 percent from the comparable 2025 weekend. The domestic total for 2026 hits $8.768 billion through Sunday.

After debuting in the top spot last weekend, Godzilla Minus Zero heads to third place with an estimated $7.5 million domestically for its sophomore frame as its North American cume is expected to hit $48.1 million. Filmmaker Takashi Yamazaki's sequel to 2023's Godzilla Minus One looks to have a sizable decline of around 75 percent.

Sony Pictures' Ramayana: Rise of a Legend is likely to notch $5.4 million in its second weekend for a domestic total of roughly $24 million through Sunday and a pleasing 38 percent drop. Its cume would rank director Nitesh Tiwari's religious epic as the second-highest-grossing Indian feature ever at the U.S. box office. The two-part movie project carries a production budget reported at $420 million and beyond.

Likely to close out the top five when final numbers are reported is A24's Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything , which continues its impressive run into its fifth weekend with around $5.1 million for the frame and a domestic total of $88.6 million. With an enviable decline of around 37 percent so deep into the run, the buzzy feature from directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim continues to build awards momentum.

Among the weekend's debuts in limited release, Neon launched James Gray's Paper Tiger in six theaters in Los Angeles and New York, with the crime drama heading to an estimated $203,000 for the frame, averaging $33,884 per screen. Adam Driver, Scarlett Johansson and Miles Teller star in the feature that Rooney's review praised as "a drama of almost overwhelming power."

Next weekend sees the arrival of Lionsgate's The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping , expected to become one of the fall's top-grossing titles.

articles.title: Chapecoense crash survivor wins promotion in final game
articles.summary: Alan Ruschel, one of six survivors in the 2016 plane crash that was carrying members of the Chapecoense team, wins promotion to Brazil‘s Serie A in his final...
articles.body:
Alan Ruschel, a survivor of the 2016 plane crash that was carrying the Chapecoense football team, won promotion to Brazil's Serie A in his final game before retirement.

Ruschel, 37, was one of just six survivors when the plane crashed in Colombia and killed 71 people, including 19 of the club's players and the coaching staff.

Despite severe injuries and spinal surgery, Ruschel returned to football a year later and retires after earning promotion to Brazil's top flight with Juventude, his boyhood club which he re-joined in 2023.

Ruschel came off the bench in the 74th minute to help see out a 2-0 win over Botafogo, resulting in an emotional farewell with a lap of honour at the club's Alfredo Jaconi Stadium.

Before the game, he was also carried into the stadium on the shoulders of fans.

"I arrived here in 2007 with the club in Serie A and I am leaving the club there as well," Ruschel told a Brazilian television station after the match.

"My body wasn't responding any more. I had two consecutive knee surgeries, so I was starting to fighting with my own body.

"It wasn't working any more, even though being on the pitch was always a pleasure."

Ruschel referenced the plane crash in a video on social media which he posted the day before the game to confirm his retirement.

"Football has given me wonderful moments, but life has put me in front of challenges that I never imagined. November 29, 2016, a day that changed my life forever.

"I lost friends, companions and people with whom I shared dreams and projects.

"And God gave me a second chance. I didn't know if I would be able to play football again, but I believed that if I was here, there was still a purpose for my life.

"And today, I have the privilege of being able to choose the moment to say goodbye."

articles.title: Johnny Depp film ‘Ebenezer’ gets actor first No. 1 opening in 8 years
articles.summary: Johnny Depp is back at the top of the box office with his first studio movie in eight years, and since fallout from a contentious libel trial against ex-wife Amber Heard left his future in Hollywood in jeopardy.
articles.body: Johnny Depp is back at the top of the box office with his first studio movie in eight years, and since fallout from a contentious libel trial against ex-wife Amber Heard left his future in Hollywood in jeopardy. But six years after he was asked to leave the “Fantastic Beasts” franchise, and three years after Depp said that he had “no further need for Hollywood,” “Ebenezer,” a Paramount Pictures release, opened in first place with about $19 million in ticket sales, according to studio estimates on Sunday. Paramount released it in 3,535 theaters. While it might be a far cry from the heights of the “Pirates of the Caribbean” franchise, which twice opened over $100 million, or even the $62 million opening of “Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald” in 2018, it is a solid start for the film, which cost a reported $38 million to produce. Internationally, it made $23 million from 63 markets, adding up to a $42 million global debut. Outside of his franchise fare, Depp more often had openings in the $20 million range (as with “Black Mass” and “Public Enemies”). The audience for “Ebenezer” was about 52% female and 81% over the age of 25, according to PostTrak exit polls. About 65% of ticket buyers said they would “definitely” recommend the film to friends. Less than half, or 47%, of the “kid” demographic (ages 12 and under) said they would tell their friends they “must see it right away.” The Charles Dickens-inspired tale is rated PG-13 and directed by Ti West, who is best known for the horror franchise X. Critics were not as warm as audiences about the film. It’s currently sitting at 52% on Rotten Tomatoes. Rupert Grint, Andrea Riseborough, Sam Claflin and Daisy Ridley also star. The question still remains as to whether this marks a major comeback for Depp, but time might tell. In exit polls, 51% of moviegoers cited Depp as their reason for attending the film. Depp’s next film, a revenge thriller called “Day Drinker,” is set for a March release from Lionsgate. Sony’s “Ghost Soldier” and Amazon MGM Studios’ “How to Rob a Bank” also opened this weekend to less fanfare. “Ghost Soldier,” an action film starring Jim Caviezel, debuted in sixth place with $5.2 million from 2,558 theaters. “How to Rob a Bank” landed in seventh place with just under $5.2 million from 2,810 theaters. Internationally, it made $5.1 million. The film from “The Fall Guy” director David Leitch had a reported net production budget of $40 million. Starring Nicholas Hoult, Zoë Kravitz and Pete Davidson, “How to Rob a Bank” did not receive good reviews. “The Cat in the Hat” landed in second place in its second weekend in theaters with $11.4 million, followed by “Godzilla Minus Zero” in third place with $8.3 million (down a whopping 73% from its opening). Fourth place went to “Ramayana: Rise of a Legend,” also in its second weekend, with $5.5 million. And the Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything” rounded out the top five with just under $5.5 million, bringing its domestic total to $89 million. “Wild Horse Nine” also added 1,075 theaters in its second weekend, where it earned $4.6 million. Jordan Firstman’s “Club Kid” had one of the best limited expansions of the year with $756,060 on 27 screens. And James Gray’s acclaimed crime thriller “Paper Tiger” opened in six locations in New York and Los Angeles to $215,009 before it expands nationwide next week. Overall it was a slower weekend than last with around $86 million in total ticket sales from North American theaters. Business should pick up next weekend, however, with the release of “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.” Top 10 movies by domestic box office With final domestic figures being released Monday, this list factors in the estimated ticket sales for Friday through Sunday at U.S. and Canadian theaters, according to Rentrak: 1. “Ebenezer,” $19 million. 2. “The Cat in the Hat,” $11.4 million. 3. “Godzilla Minus Zero,” $8.3 million. 4. “Ramayana: Rise of a Legend,” $5.5 million. 5. “You Can See Everything,” $5.5 million. 6. “Ghost Soldier,” $5.2 million. 7. “How to Rob a Bank,” $5.2 million. 8. “Wild Horse Nine,” $4.6 million. 9. “Wildwood,” $4.5 million. 10. “Clayface,” $3.7 million.

articles.title: Phil Collins Says He’s a ‘Well Man’ Now and Hints at the ‘Possibility of Doing Some Shows’ Amid Health Battle: ‘You Haven’t Heard the Last of Me’
articles.summary: Phil Collins made a rare public appearance to accept his induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame at the ceremony in Los Angeles on Saturday, where he add...
articles.body:
Phil Collins made a rare public appearance to accept his induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame at the ceremony in Los Angeles on Saturday, where he addressed his health, calling himself "a well man now."

"Thank you so much. Thank you. I'm really not as bad as it looks. I'm much better," Collins said at the beginning of his speech. "I've got to say, there are lots of rumors about whether I'm going to sing, do a tour of an album, but you haven't heard the last of me," he added.

In the press room after the ceremony, he explained that he has an in-house recording studio and a band of fellow musicians that make it possible — and even enjoyable — for him to keep making music. He hopes to share this music and tour down the road.

"Everything started to go wrong," the musician said. "So at one point I didn't think I'd live, let alone go on the road again. But just the other night I was talking to the kids about it, and everyone got excited, including myself, that it's not beyond the realm of possibility of doing some shows."

"I've got some great friends of mine that are great musicians that have been in my band. And I'd like to get down to my studio just to have some fun and write some music that I hope will be good enough for people to hear and sort of enjoy," he added. "So it's a work in progress."

Collins has often been open about his health issues. He told The Times of London in August that he almost died in 2024 from health complications stemming from alcohol abuse. In early 2026, he told BBC Two that he's undergone five surgeries on his knee.

Despite his health challenges, he is determined to continue his music career. "Well, you say something once and you gotta answer questions about it forever. I can't believe that I'm not going to do something. I'm not very good at doing nothing," Collins told reporters.

articles.title: 'The Odyssey' actor John Leguizamo demands Democrats 'abolish ICE,' shut down detention centers
articles.summary: Actor John Leguizamo's Instagram video demands abolishing ICE, shutting down detention centers and ending the Electoral College in a sweeping policy list.
articles.body: "The Odyssey" actor John Leguizamo urged Democrats to abolish Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), shut down detention centers and protect abortion rights and transgender Americans on Friday, while outlining his priorities for the next Congress. Leguizamo presented a lengthy list of demands in a video he posted on social media, along with an accompanying policy list aimed at lawmakers taking office in January. His immigration proposals also included protecting sanctuary cities, ending family separation and pursuing immigration reform. "Alright, my project 2027, starting January 3rd: Get it done, Dems, all right? Guarantee affordable healthcare, Medicare for all, strengthen social security, abolish ICE, shut down detention centers, end family separation, immigration reform, protect sanctuary cities, comprehensive gun reform," he said in the video. JEFFRIES VOWS DEMOCRATS WON’T ‘GIVE A DIME’ TO TRUMP’S DEPORTATION EFFORTS "Trial, and convict Stephen Miller for ICE murders, impeach Todd Blanche, end Citizens United, so there's no dark money in government," Leguizamo added. Leguizamo’s agenda also extended to changes in presidential powers, elections and the Supreme Court. He called for eliminating the Electoral College, limiting presidential pardon powers, ending presidential immunity and establishing term limits for Supreme Court justices. His economic priorities included a $20 federal minimum wage, a billionaire wealth tax, paid maternity leave and a 10% cap on credit card interest rates. DEMOCRATS’ MIDTERM SWEEP OPENS PATH TO BYPASSING ELECTORAL COLLEGE BY 2028 The actor's demand to close detention centers overlaps with legislation already proposed by Democratic lawmakers, although Leguizamo's list did not provide the implementation details outlined in those bills. Rep. Delia Ramirez, D-Ill., and Rep. Yvette Clarke, D-N.Y., introduced the Melt ICE Act in January. According to Ramirez’s office, it would remove immigration detention authorities from federal law and terminate existing detention contracts within two years of enactment. Her office outlined how the legislation would redirect the agency’s funding. "Redirects ICE funding to community-based organizations to provide wrap-around services to communities around the country," her office said in its summary of the bill. The proposal would also prohibit new detention contracts and require DHS to submit a plan to remove immigrants from ankle monitors within six months. Funding would instead go toward community services, including housing and health care. 'SQUAD' DEMOCRAT SLAMMED BY TRUMP ADMIN FOR MOST 'RADICAL' PLAN TARGETING ICE YET Ramirez subsequently announced a broader proposal, the Reimagining Safety Act, to dismantle DHS and replace it with a Department of Community Safety. Her office described a plan to abolish ICE and Customs and Border Protection while preserving customs functions and agencies responsible for disaster response, transportation security and cybersecurity. Support for cutting ICE funding is not universal among Democrats. Rep. Henry Cuellar, D-Texas, previously opposed defunding. "I don't believe in defunding ICE," Cuellar said, in a previous statement to Fox News Digital. Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y.; and Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., while calling for new Democratic leadership. "My project 2027 starts Jan 3! If you have the cojones to sign on Dems and reps with wisdom. No more absences (means u Pelosi) no excuses! Enough is enough and if you can’t wrangle your peeps Hakeem then bye! ✌bye anyway you are compromised! And Schumer u too should go away! We need new leadership," the actor posted. Fox News Digital reached out to the offices of Pelosi, Jeffries, and Schumer for comment, but did not immediately hear back. Leguizamo’s latest demands followed an earlier appeal the actor made to his own audience. In January, he told followers who supported ICE to stop attending his performances and watching his films. DEMS SEIZE ON MIDTERM ROUT TO DEMAND ICE REFORM, BUT POLLS REVEAL A TWIST IN WHO PRIORITIZED IMMIGRATION"If you follow ICE, unfollow me, don’t come to my shows, and don’t watch my movies," Leguizamo said. A DHS spokesperson told Fox News Digital that DHS law enforcement has been delivering on President Donald Trump's promises since day one. "Since Day One, DHS law enforcement has been delivering on President Trump’s promise to the American people to arrest and deport criminal illegal aliens including murderers, rapists, pedophiles, gang members, and terrorists," the spokesperson said. "Nearly 60% of ICE arrests are of illegal aliens charged or convicted of a crime in the U.S. More than three million illegal aliens are out of the country and counting. Our message is clear: if you come to our country illegally, we will find you, we will arrest you, and we will deport you," the spokesperson told Fox News Digital. Because of smears like this, our ICE officers are now facing a 1,600% increase in assaults, a 3,300% increase in vehicle attacks, and an 8,000% increase in death threats," the spokesperson added. The White House told Fox News Digital that Leguizamo was "out of touch" with Americans. "This C-list Hollywood actor is out of touch with Americans. articles.title: Beauty queen stripped of Miss USA crown over hidden husband, kids gets unexpected spotlight decades later
articles.summary: Justus Kelley honors Mary Leona Gage, who lost her Miss USA crown in 1957 for being married with children, as she prepares for Miss Universe.
articles.body: Nearly 70 years ago, a beauty queen lost her Miss USA crown after pageant officials learned she was married and had children. In August, Justus Kelley broke that barrier, becoming the first married woman and mother to win the title during the pageant's 75th edition. Kelley, 31, is a foster mother who founded the nonprofit Foster Footprints to support children and families involved in foster care. The historic victory came three years after the Miss USA pageant changed its rules to allow married women and mothers to compete. Kelley is scheduled to compete in the 75th Miss Universe pageant, which is set to take place Nov. 24 in Puerto Rico. FORMER MISS USA CONTESTANT MADE A LIFE-CHANGING DECISION AT 26 AFTER CANCER DEVASTATED FAMILY Kelley paid tribute to Gage by wearing a custom black-and-white coat featuring the former beauty queen's image as she traveled to Puerto Rico for the competition. "Having the opportunity to represent the United States on the Miss Universe stage, I couldn't help but think about Mary Leona Gage and the circumstances under which she represented this organization," Kelley, 31, told People magazine. "She was a woman who, in many ways, wasn't allowed to be fully herself or embrace all that she was. Her title was ultimately taken away because society wasn't ready to accept who she was as a wife and mother of two." On Aug. 27, the Miss USA Organization held the 75th edition of the national pageant in Miami. Kelley, who held the title of Miss Virginia USA 2026, succeeded 2025 winner Audrey Eckert. The pageant began allowing married women and mothers to compete in 2023. WATCH: MISS USA 2026 REVEALS HOW SHE TRAINED FOR PAGEANT WITH KIDS IN TOW In 1957, Gage represented Maryland in the Miss USA pageant and won the title, according to People. Shortly after Gage's win, rumors circulated about her marital status and children. Gage initially denied the reports. However, it was later revealed that she had married at 14 and given birth to her first child soon afterward. She had her second child at 16, The Baltimore Sun reported. Gage also misrepresented her age, telling pageant officials she was 21 when she was actually 18. Following an official investigation, Gage was disqualified and stripped of her Miss USA crown. Runner-up Charlotte Sheffield, who represented Utah, assumed the crown and received the prizes. Gage, who lost the crown about 24 hours after her win, said she received hate mail following her disqualification. Gage had already competed in the Miss Universe preliminary round and secured a spot among the 15 semifinalists before she was disqualified. Although Sheffield inherited the Miss USA crown, she could not replace Gage in the international competition because preliminary judging had already concluded. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS According to The Baltimore Sun, Gage later worked as a performer at the Tropicana Hotel in Las Vegas and reportedly dated Frank Sinatra and former Mr. Universe Mickey Hargitay. She also pursued a film career but never achieved widespread success. Despite losing her crown, Gage continued watching the Miss USA pageant every year. She died in 2010 at age 71. Kelley told People that Gage has been on her mind as she prepares for the Miss Universe competition. "I think about how much has changed since then, and how grateful I am that today's American women have the opportunity to represent their country while embracing every part of who they are," Kelley said. articles.title: Listen to this: Armand Hammer’s Snakes & Ladders
articles.summary: Armand Hammer’s latest album, Snakes & Ladders, is among their best.
articles.body: I open with this caveat: I haven’t had a ton of time to digest the surprise Armand Hammer record that dropped this week. Billy Woods and Elucid rarely miss, though, and my initial reaction is that Snakes & Ladders ranks among their best. It doesn’t have the seamless throughline production-wise that their collabs with Alchemist (Haram and Mercy) do, but it’s still clearly the singular vision of the two men at its center. Ominous noises dance in the background, blasts of noise add dashes of industrial rage, bass lines throb, and saxophone bleats call out to the sky. Woods and Elucid have always had excellent taste in production, but here they seem to have brought out the best in collaborators like clipping, Kenny Segal, and Child Actor. They’ve also successfully rallied them around a specific sound palette that keeps the record from actually sounding like it has beats from 11 different producers. [Media: Of course, what makes Armand Hammer stand out from many of their contemporaries is their unique and verbose flows. Their lyrical mastery even makes guest rappers like $ilkmoney, who you can practically hear stalking around the mic as he seethes on “Risk,” up their game. On songs like “Gravity,” Billy Woods navigates burgeoning romance with shocking directness, while also acknowledging obliquely how hard it can be to say what you mean. > Get it off your chest or put it to the side As a preface, all due respect, I suggest ‘Cause it’s nothing more precious than time On “Vespers,” he references Siouxsie and the Banshees and says “My nightcap three fingers of Fernet,” which is probably the first time I’ve ever heard Fernet Branca get a shoutout in a rap song. “Graveside” is another highlight where it’s Elucid’s turn to get vulnerable: > I see you in the grave, I see you in the dirt Shouts and hollers every which way, hurting Darkness chase light Steel shut close curtain In some ways, this record feels like a culmination of what Billy Woods and Elucid have been working towards on their non-Alchemist-produced Armand Hammer records like We Buy Diabetic Test Strips, but also their recent solo records like Golliwog and Revelator. articles.title: Russell Brand says ‘I am not guilty’ in statement from prison read by his wife
articles.summary: Russell Brand declared “I am not guilty” in a new statement read by his wife on his YouTube channel Sunday, days after a London court sentenced him to prison on rape and sexual assault charges.
articles.body: Russell Brand declared “I am not guilty” in a new statement read by his wife on his YouTube channel Sunday, days after a London court sentenced him to prison on rape and sexual assault charges. The 51-year-old comedian and former actor was sentenced Nov. 9 to 10 1/2 years in prison after a London court found him guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. He pleaded not guilty to all counts and denied all of the allegations. In a new YouTube video, Brand’s wife, Laura Brand, read the statement on his behalf. “So, Russell has asked me to read something to you today: ‘Beloved brothers and sisters in Christ, God bless you for your support. As you know, I am not guilty for the offenses I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening,’” she said. “I am incarcerated in HMP Littlehey. ... I’m in the biggest sex offenders prison in Europe. The good news is that I have already seen that the staff here are strong, they are kind, and they are dedicated,” she continued, reading his statement. “And as for my fellow prisoners, I now know that I am in no position to judge anyone. I don’t know which other men here are not guilty, and the ones that are, they are people that Christ died to save, like you and me. Let us all love, pray for, and forgive one another as God forgave us,” the statement said. Brand closed by asking the public to support his wife and family. “I feel your prayers,” the statement said. Brand’s YouTube channel features Christian-themed content, including a “Sunday Service” series he hosts with his wife. At the start of the video, Laura Brand said she would continue the series. Sunday’s episode included prerecorded video of the couple discussing faith and morality. “Even though it’s painful, and obviously will take some getting used to for me to even sit here and not have my my companion, my person, with me, but I want to continue,” she said. Justice Joel Bennathan called Brand a “sexual predator” before delivering his sentence. At sentencing, Brand’s victims shared in-person and written statements about the trauma and its effects on their daily lives. Brand was convicted of raping a female fan at his home in 2009 after she met him at one of his shows. He was also found guilty of sexually assaulting three other women: one whose breasts he grabbed at a party in 2004; one who said he kissed and groped her at a London radio station in 2004 or 2005; and one who said he pressed his face into her groin during the recording of an advertisement in 2009. He was found not guilty of two other counts of rape and one count of attempted indecent assault. The sentence marked a stunning fall from grace for Brand, who rose to fame as a broadcaster and stand-up comedian and went on to a Hollywood career, starring in films including “Forgetting Sarah Marshall” and “Get Him to the Greek.” If you or someone you know has been sexually assaulted, call the National Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-800-656-4673. articles.title: Aroldo Macêdo, guitarrista baiano falecido aos 68 anos, contribuiu para perpetuar a sonoridade do trio elétrico | G1
articles.body:
Filho de Osmar Macedo (1923 – 1997), Aroldo Macêdo (1958 – 2026) morre aos 68 anos na cidade natal de Salvador (BA) — Foto: Felipe Oliveira / Divulgação

♬ A morte de Aroldo Macêdo (23 de fevereiro de 1958 – 15 de novembro de 2026) – ocorrida ontem, domingo, em Salvador (BA), por causa de doença neurodegenerativa diagnosticada em dezembro de 2025 – tira de cena um instrumentista relevante no universo da música baiana.

Filho de Osmar Macedo (1923 – 1997), criador do trio elétrico em 1950 juntamente com Adolfo Nascimento (1920 – 1978), o Dodô, Aroldo tinha 68 anos e era irmão de Armadinho Macedo, ás da guitarra baiana e do bandolim.

Assim como os irmãos músicos Armandinho, André e Betinho, Aroldo Macêdo foi herdeiro musical da proeza elétrica de Dodô & Osmar. Músico polivalente, Aroldo Macêdo tocava vários instrumentos, mas foi no habilidoso manejo da guitarra baiana que ele ajudou a preservar a sonoridade do trio elétrico.

“A contribuição de Aroldo para o desenvolvimento da segunda guitarra do trio elétrico imprimiu uma marca própria à tradição musical que a família dele ajudou a construir”, sintetizou o Ministério da Cultura em nota de pesar sobre a morte do artista.

Antes de se fixar na guitarra, Aroldo Macêdo tocou piano – instrumento que aprendeu a tocar ainda na infância – e, na adolescência, incursionou pela bateria, instrumento que também continuou tocando na vida adulta.

Como músico, arranjador, compositor e produtor musical, Aroldo Macêdo transitou por gêneros como frevo (com tempero baiano), choro, rock e até bossa nova. Como compositor, Aroldo deixa cancioneiro autoral que inclui várias parcerias com Moraes Moreira (1947 – 2020), primeiro cantor a se apresentar em um trio elétrico em 1977.

Dentre as parcerias de Aroldo com Moraes, há “A lira e Jandira” (1977), “Cantor do trio” (1980), “Cochabamba” (1977), “Mulher e cidade – Marília” (1981) e “Vida e Carnaval” (1980).

Aroldo Macedo também teve atuação relevante como educador, pois, a partir de 2007, passou a conduzir a Oficina de música instrumental Osmar Macêdo, escola de música pioneira por oferecer aulas de guitarra baiana.

articles.title: Fans cheer as AO3 nears full return after security incident
articles.summary: In a comeback tale like one from Harry Potter battling back his nemesis or a “Heated Rivalry” hockey hero rebounding from injury, a top global fandom site that was sidelined by a security incident is now on the mend.
articles.body: In a comeback tale like one from Harry Potter battling back his nemesis or a “Heated Rivalry” hockey hero rebounding from injury, a top global fandom site that was sidelined by a security incident is now on the mend. The activist group behind the popular Archive of Our Own, or AO3, platform, a collaborative online space which serves up fans’ spinoff narratives derived from well-known published stories, says it’s undergoing a limited return after a shutdown on Oct. 29. “AO3 is now up!” said a status page for the Organization for Transformative Works, an activist group behind the platform, on Sunday. The outage sent fans of the platform — readers and authors alike — into a desperate void for the past two weeks, with a “Bad Gateway” message stirring frustration. Some authors were outraged when readers uploaded their works to Google Drive and other platforms without their permission during the outage. The return drew many expressions of joy Sunday. The organization, in a summary it posted on Instagram of its 2025 results, said nearly 2.6 million AO3 works were created, with nearly 40 billion page views. Nearly 2 million accounts have been created, it said. AO3 hasn’t been without its critics, who have warned about sexual content that could be available to minors and fandom racism through the platform. The group said some features like user icons have been disabled and importing of external work isn’t available, while downloads are currently only possible in the web-language HTML format. It promised those features will ultimately return. “We understand that the wait and uncertainty surrounding AO3’s return have been difficult, and we apologize for the inconvenience,” the status update said. The organization hasn’t specified the cause of the security incident, but at least one expert says AI-enabled exploits might have been a factor. Mel Stanfill, a professor at the University of Central Florida who has written about the challenges of content moderation at scale with an all-volunteer team, hailed the “relatively quick” return and compared the outage to a recent one at Microsoft — which has far more resources and paid staff. Stanfill, who volunteers for an academic journal run by the organization but does not speak on its behalf, said in an email that such security incidents “are likely to continue to happen in the age of AI-enabled coding as the finding and exploiting of exploits is scaled up rapidly.” He noted that “it is difficult even for organizations with billions in revenue to solve these problems.” From fanfic to podfic: New media emerge In late October, the team predicted that the security incident would take up to four weeks for AO3 to get back up, while floating the prospect of a partial revival “in a degraded state” — which appears to be what was taking place on Sunday. The organization said contributors’ “works, bookmarks, kudos, etc., are still safe” and that no drafts were deleted during the outage — but it couldn’t rule out that the user database might have been compromised. AO3 is a hub of content from fans who have produced content that riffs off fiction, art and other culture and entertainment: Imagine a repository of sequels, prequels and derivatives dreamt up by adoring aficionados of some of the world’s best-known titles. The result is catchy products like “fanfic” — fiction from fans — and similar fanart, as well as “podfics,” readings of narratives shared in audio form. A recent listing of “ship stats” — or the number of references to relationships of stars from literature — shows that pairings of characters featured in the Harry Potter, Heated Rivalry and anime fandoms were the most prominent this summer. The platform, which is run by volunteers, went fully public in 2009, and has shown strong user growth: In June, the Organization for Transformative Works said AO3 had 11 million registered users — up from 10 million four months earlier. It said the archive was nearing 18 million works. The reaction from many fans of the fandom platform was swift and exuberant about its return. “So, we’ve all agreed we don’t need to sleep tonight, now that AO3 is finally back, right? Right!?” quipped a user going by the name of yet.another.loon on the Threads social media site. User Verkielos gushed: “Just got email from AO3 about a fic update. The world is healing!”

articles.summary: Actress Julianne Moore has expressed excitement about the continuation of 'The Hunger Games' franchise, saying she looks forward to watching the upcoming
articles.body: Actress Julianne Moore has expressed excitement about the continuation of 'The Hunger Games' franchise, saying she looks forward to watching the upcoming prequel 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping', which is set to arrive in theatres later this month, according to People.Moore, 65, who portrayed President Alma Coin in the original film saga, shared her thoughts on the franchise's latest instalment during an exclusive interview with People."I'm excited to go [see it]," Moore said about 'Sunrise on the Reaping', which is set 24 years before the events of the original story and follows a teenage Haymitch Abernathy during the 50th Hunger Games."It opens around Thanksgiving. That's Hunger Games time," she added with a laugh, referring to the franchise's tradition of releasing its films around the end of November, coinciding with the annual holiday.Based on the bestselling book series by Suzanne Collins, 'The Hunger Games' follows a dozen districts that are required to select one boy and one girl, aged between 12 and 18, to compete in an annual event in which 24 participants fight until only one remains, according to People.Moore appeared as President Alma Coin, the leader of District 13 and the head of the second rebellion against the Capitol, in 'The Hunger Games: Mockingjay - Part 1' (2014) and 'The Hunger Games: Mockingjay - Part 2' (2015).The original film series began with 'The Hunger Games' in 2012, followed by 'The Hunger Games: Catching Fire' in 2013. It featured Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson, Liam Hemsworth, Donald Sutherland, Elizabeth Banks, Stanley Tucci, Lenny Kravitz, Philip Seymour Hoffman and Sam Claflin, alongside Moore and Woody Harrelson.Reflecting on her experience working on the two 'Mockingjay' films, the Oscar-winning actress said she had fond memories of the cast and crew."I think it was just working with all those fantastic people. I love them," she said.Speaking particularly about Jennifer Lawrence, who played Katniss Everdeen in the original films, Moore added, "I just think she's so funny. She's so talented.""She was a great Katniss, and I love to watch her in everything," she further said.The franchise expanded with its first prequel, 'The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes', released in 2023. The film followed a young Coriolanus Snow, played by Tom Blyth, who was assigned to mentor tribute Lucy Gray Baird, portrayed by Rachel Zegler, during the 10th annual Hunger Games. The late Donald Sutherland played Snow in the first four films, while Ralph Fiennes takes over the role in the upcoming prequel.'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' will see Joseph Zada portray a younger version of Haymitch Abernathy, originally played by Woody Harrelson, during his participation in the 50th Hunger Games. Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson will also reprise their roles as Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark, respectively.The upcoming film is scheduled to release in theatres on November 20, as per the outlet.Moore, meanwhile, continues her partnership with Eli Lilly for its Brain Health Matters campaign.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Daniel Hall, co-founder of the Australian band Taxiride, passes away at 48
articles.summary: Australian musician Daniel Hall, co-founder of the band Taxiride, has sadly passed away at the age of 48. Join fans and loved ones in remembering his incredible talent and legacy in the music industry.
articles.body: Famed musician Daniel Hall, who was best known as one of the founding members of the rock band Taxiride, has passed away. The news of Hall’s death was shared online through the band’s official social media channels. Accordingly he left for his heavenly abode on November 13.Daniel Hall passes away at 48Taxiride took to their Facebook account to share the news of their bandmate’s passing. The post read, "It is with the heaviest of hearts we announce the passing of our youngest brother in arms, Daniel James Hall. We shared some amazing experiences, and his departure doesn’t seem real. Rest In Peace, Dan.” The post was accompanied by a throwback photo of Hall from his early days with the band.Hall’s partner, Jess, also shared a condolence post on the musician’s personal page, which read, “I am completely devastated. Your prayers and kind messages are appreciated.” At the time of writing, they did not share what happened to the famed musician.Tributes pour in for Daniel HallThe comment section under the post announcing his passing was filled with condolence messages, with many fans also sharing their fond memories of interacting with the artist and the band’s music. One person wrote, “So saddened to hear Mum came and told me because we knew Dan when we were little, as we had a mutual friend. Dan and I bonded over being born the exact same day. Years later, when his band, Taxiride, started, it was a thrill for all of us seeing a friend succeed, and when CD released, I brought a copy. Rest well, my twin brother.” Another person wrote, “This is such devastating news. Love you, Dan. RIP.”Another social media user fondly remembered Hall and shared, “Oh no, it was only recently I had spoken with Dan over messages about some great tire memories I have and his other music. Such a talent. Sending my love to all of you.”Who was Daniel Hall?Daniel Hall was born in 1978 and was the co-founder, bassist, pianist, and vocalist of the Australian rock band Taxiride. The group is best known for songs like ‘Imaginate’ and ‘Get Set.’ He is also credited with forming the band Airway Lanes.Taxiride started in the late 90s after Tim Watson and Tim Wild started working together. Later, Jason Singh and Hall joined the duo, and the four of them started their career by busking in public. They made their debut in 1999 and were an instant success, with their debut album and songs charting at the top of many music charts. Hall worked with the band till 2001, after which he dropped out of the group and started another band, Airway Lanes.He joined Taxiride again after some time, and since then the group has been together and performing across the world. The band still has some shows scheduled, though it has not been announced whether they will be cancelled altogether or rescheduled.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
